item.title: Public Policy Manager
item.description: JOB SUMMARY: The Manager of Public Policy is a member of Truth Initiative's Public Policy team and advances the organization's policy priorities by conducting strategic policy research and analysis; monitoring and evaluating legislative, regulatory, and public health developments related to nicotine and substance use, cannabis, opioids, and other emerging public health issues; developing policy reports, issue briefs; and supporting policy advocacy efforts through research, coalition engagement, and stakeholder education. In addition to contributing to work on nicotine and tobacco issues, The Manager serves as a subject matter expert on substance use and addiction policy issues and works collaboratively across Truth Initiative to translate complex policy developments into actionable insights, evidence-based recommendations, and audience-appropriate materials. DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (*ESSENTIAL DUTIES): Monitor, research, and analyze federal, state, and local legislation, regulations, and policy developments related to nicotine and tobacco, substance use prevention, cannabis regulation, opioid misuse and overdose prevention, addiction treatment, and related public health issues.* Identify policy trends, emerging issues, and opportunities for organizational engagement, public education, and policy impact.* Produce policy analyses, issue briefs, fact sheets, regulatory summaries, white papers, reports, and other written products.* Draft and support the development of formal comments to federal and state agencies.* Synthesize scientific literature, policy research, surveillance data, and public health evidence into actionable policy recommendations.* Attend and report on hearings, regulatory meetings, policy briefings, and conferences.* Build and maintain relationships with external partners, coalitions, public health organizations, academic institutions, and governmental agencies. Represent Truth Initiative in external meetings, working groups, coalitions, and professional conferences. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Master's degree in Public Policy, Public Health, Health Policy, Political Science, Law, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. 5-7 years of professional experience in public policy, government affairs, health policy, public health advocacy, regulatory affairs, or policy research and analysis. Demonstrated experience in substance use prevention policy, opioid policy, cannabis policy, addiction treatment policy, behavioral health policy, and tobacco control policy. Preferred candidate would have previous exposure to substance use prevention world and contacts Experience monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory activity at the federal and/or state levels. Excellent public health policy research and analytical skills. Strong writing, editing, and policy communication skills. Ability to interpret legislation, regulations, scientific evidence, and public health data. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. PREFFERED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience working on federal public health, substance use, healthcare, behavioral health, or regulatory policy issues. Familiarity with federal legislative and regulatory processes and agencies including FDA, CDC, SAMHSA, NIH, CMS, DEA, ONDCP, and HHS. Experience drafting or contributing to public comments, Congressional briefings, policy recommendations, or regulatory analyses. Experience engaging with federal agencies, Congressional offices, national advocacy organizations, or public health coalitions. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This position is based in Washington, D.C. with a hybrid work schedule of three days in the office and two telework days. COMPENSATION PACKAGE: The salary range for this role is starting at $85,000-$90,000 per year on a national basis. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to qualifications for the role, relevant work experience, skillset, internal equity, location, and certifications, consistent with applicable law. Salary is just one part of our total rewards package which additionally includes performance bonus for eligible roles, and competitive benefits. Interested candidates should submit their cover letter and resume here OR mail application materials to: Human Resources Attn: Public Policy Manager 900 G Street, NW Fourth Floor Washington, DC 20001 Fax: (202) 204-5214 No telephone calls please. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status or disability.

item.title: Deputy Director Public Policy Legislative Engagement
item.description: ABOUT OUR CLIENT: Talent Road's client is a national nonprofit and field builder with the mission of improving lives by empowering students with essential skills and dispositions for making better decisions. Founded in 2014 and backed by experts in decision sciences, business, and education-including several Nobel laureates-our client believes that better decisions lead to better lives and a better society. They partner with teachers, academic and business leaders, families, and community members to raise awareness and lead the growing call to have Decision Education taught in schools nationwide. They are committed to an inclusive, supportive, and collaborative culture. Their diverse team comprises educators, researchers, subject matter experts, and other professionals dedicated to the mission. JOB OVERVIEW: The Deputy Director of Public Policy, Legislative Engagement is a senior role responsible for advancing the state and national policy agenda by coordinating legislative engagement, managing policy‑aligned outreach, and assisting with coalition and stakeholder activities that advance Decision Education. This position focuses on legislative strategy, drafting policy documents, cultivating relationships through meetings and events, state-level lobbying and advocacy, and ensuring effective communication with policymakers, external partners, and internal teams. The Deputy Director of Public Policy, Legislative Engagement will report to the Director of Public Policy (DPP) within the Public Policy Department, which is responsible for advancing state and national policy priorities to support the adoption and expansion of Decision Education. WHAT YOU WILL DO: Legislative Engagement Lead implementation of the Alliance's direct and indirect lobbying strategies in partnership with the Director of Public Policy, cultivating relationships with governors' offices, state departments of education, state boards of education, and state legislative bodies, as well as with relevant think tanks, coalitions, advocacy organizations, and trade associations. Proactively monitor, analyze, and influence key policymaker activity and legislation at the st ate and regional levels. Draft legislative memoranda, policy memoranda, and legislator education and communication materials. Translate complex federal and state education bills, administrative rules, and public budget allocations into actionable policy briefs, testimonies, and memos. Engage current and past Policymaker Fellows in the design and implementation of legislation, regulations, and pilot programs in collaboration with the Senior Manager, Public Policy. Manage relationships and contracts with retained lobbying firms in key states. Strategic Planning and Management Build regional policy, advocacy, and lobbying plans in conjunction with the Director of Public Policy, contracted lobbyists, and regional partners. Support the development and monitoring of department-level Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) related to policy development and adoption. Collaborate with the communications team, DPP, and other teams to design research briefings and public-facing toolkits that shape the national narrative around the importance of Decision Education in K-12 education policy. Support senior‑level relationship management with key strategic policy leaders, including preparation, alignment, and follow‑up for high‑value engagements. Track staff and stakeholder engagement efforts in Salesforce, Wrike, and other project management tools. Collaborate with internal teams to ensure public policy activities are aligned, supported, and communicated effectively. Design and facilitate necessary legislative training and professional development for staff and volunteers who engage in public policy opportunities and engagements. WHAT YOU NEED: At least 8 years of progressive experience leading legislative advocacy, public policy formulation, and lobbying initiatives, with a clear focus on the education sector. Deep expertise in legislative processes, state-level education governance, and public K-12 financing structures. Experience managing complex cross-sector initiatives, public policy campaigns, and education policy lobbying initiatives. Experience using a CRM system. ADDITIONAL INFORMTION: Compensation: $110,000 - $140,000 annually Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (100% employer paid) Life Insurance (100% employer paid) Long Term Disability Insurance (100% employer paid) Employee Assistance Program 401K Retirement Plan with up to a 5% match Flexible Spending Account Up to 20 Days of Paid Time Off in your first year (prorated based on your start date) Shortened Friday workweeks and select summer months Hybrid work schedule – Office location: Bala Cynwyd, PA This position is open to both local and remote candidates. Local team members are expected to follow a hybrid schedule, working onsite at our headquarters in Bala Cynwyd, PA, on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with remote work permitted on other business days. Fully remote employees are expected to maintain a productive home-based work environment and remain actively engaged in team operations during East Coast hours. Additionally, the role requires 30-50 percent travel, including stakeholder and legislative engagements, travel to state capitals, national conferences, and to internal and all-staff meetings at organization headquarters.

item.title: Congressional Liaison Officer N2701
item.description: Position is 100% Onsite Who We Are : Founded in 2007, SimIS Inc. is an innovative information technology solution Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) that models future environments, requirements, and capabilities, and then secures the enterprise from internal and external threats compliant with Federal, State, and industry standard governance to ensure client mission success. Our performance standard is “excellence,” with an outcomes-based, quality focus in our services and products, guided by our core values of honesty (in word and deed), relationships (confidence and trust with clients and partners), teamwork (shared goals, mission, and purpose), loyalty (allegiance to our client and team), and importance of others (work and win as a team). SimIS is currently recruiting for the listed position and is contingent upon award. The position is anticipated to be “on site.” Job Description: SimIS, Inc. is seeking provides support for the role of Liaison Officer to the U.S. Congress to serve as our customers forward presence in Washington, D.C., representing interests, monitoring legislative dynamics, and cultivating strong relationships with Members of Congress, staffers, and relevant committees. SimIS, Inc. seeks a Congressional Liaison Officer to ensure our customers visibility on Capitol Hill, strengthening their network within the U.S. legislative branch, and supporting efforts to anticipate and adapt to U.S. defense priorities. Qualifications: Master's degree in Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Law, or a similar field. BS degree with significant Congressional staff experience will be considered. Five years of experience working with or within the U.S. Congress, particularly on defense, appropriations, and foreign policy issues. In-depth knowledge of the U.S. Congressional process, including authorization and appropriations cycles. A proven track record of success in a government relations position, with a demonstrated ability to manage a legislative portfolio, understand and communicate complex policies, and successfully navigate the legislative process. Excellent communication skills, particularly the ability to interface effectively with elected officials, policymakers, and key Congressional and federal staff, verbally, in writing, and through professional interpersonal skills, to inform, educate, and persuade in support of defense initiatives. Ability to work and communicate with colleagues across departments to gather the resources, skills, and expertise necessary to convey the customers message on Capitol Hill and across administrations. Ability to represent and advocate the organization's policy positions to Congress, the Executive Branch, think tanks, and other relevant stakeholders. Ability to develop and implement long- and short-term action plans that lead to the accomplishment of initiatives on innovation, capability development, and other assigned topics. Responsibilities: Monitor and analyze the U.S. defense budget process, from planning to execution, highlighting implications for NATO. Track ongoing Congressional defense reforms and assess their impact on NATO transformation. Provide strategic reporting on Congressional debates and decisions concerning Ukraine and broader Euro-Atlantic security. Assess budget issues linked to the U.S. troop presence in Europe, with specific attention to burden-sharing debates. Analyse the political dynamics of defense-related legislation, identifying key influencers and agendas. Plan and conduct informal engagements, including dinners and meetings, with legislators and staffers to promote ACT visibility. Monitor legislative initiatives, hearings, and committee activities relevant to NATO. Manage relationships with Members of Congress and provide tailored briefings on ACT and NATO priorities. Coordinate with U.S. executive agencies, NATO missions, and Allied embassies to ensure message coherence. Produce regular reports for SACT and POLAD on Congressional trends, risks, and opportunities.. Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision Short-Term Disability (at no cost to you) & Long-Term Disability Life Insurance 401(k) Savings Plan Flex Spending Accounts Tuition Assistance Program Professional Development Paid Time Off (PTO) 11 Federal Holidays each year SimIS, Inc. is an EOE / M / F / Disability / VET / Drug Free Employer
item.dc:creator: SimIS

item.title: Legislative Auditor Mid East Tennessee
item.description: Legislative Auditor: Mid-east Tennessee Location: Mid-east Tennessee (Putnam, Cumberland, White, Van Buren, Bledsoe, and Warren counties) Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot This position conducts external audits for local government entities in the Mid-east Tennessee region, ensuring accountability, transparency, and effective operations across publicly funded organizations. Responsibilities may include examining and reviewing records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for state and local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Why You'll Love This Job Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek Opportunities for professional growth and development Collaborative and supportive team environment Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do Conduct audits of state and local governmental entities in accordance with professional auditing standards. Examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices. Evaluate financial statement presentation, internal controls, compliance, and operational efficiency and effectiveness. Produce clear, logical, and well-supported workpapers and data analyses. Communicate clearly with auditees, coworkers, elected officials, and stakeholders. Take initiative, seek continuous improvement, and contribute to a collaborative team culture. What We're Looking For Required: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Business Administration with at least 24 semester hours in accounting Ability to learn quickly, think critically, problem solve, and produce accurate work Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Clear written and verbal communication skills Ability to work tactfully with coworkers, auditees, and stakeholders Sound judgment in evaluating situations and making decisions Preferred: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license (not required but strongly encouraged for advancement) Experience in auditing, governmental accounting, or related fields Logistics Travel: For Local Government Auditors, travel is required but is generally confined to same day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays may be required, as necessary. Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. About the Office The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury audits state and local government entities and oversees financial and administrative management of state government. We are nationally recognized for professionalism and accountability and consistently rank as a Top Workplace. Learn more at www.comptroller.tn.gov Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to fair and equal employment opportunities and maintaining a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, veteran status, or any category protected by law. NOTICE This position requires a criminal background check. You may be required to provide information about your criminal history to be considered for this position. Texting TOS and Privacy Policy: Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. After you send the SMS message "STOP" to us, we will send you an SMS message to confirm that you have been unsubscribed. After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. If you want to join again, just sign up as you did the first time and we will start sending SMS messages to you again. If you are experiencing issues with the messaging program, you can reply with the keyword HELP for more assistance, or you can get help directly at ig.askhr@cot.tn.gov . Message frequency will vary depending on the application process. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Msg & data rates may apply. If you have any questions about your text plan or data plan, it is best to contact your wireless provider. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy below. Privacy Policy: We collect your mobile number and related opt-in data for the delivery of SMS messages. Your mobile opt-in data and consent will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

item.title: Franklin County Election Canvasser
item.description: The Opportunity Down Home North Carolina (DHNC) seeks field canvassers in Franklin County to aid in our 2026 field campaigns. This year, Down Home members will endorse multiple candidates for office who align with our values and vision for a North Carolina that works for all working folks. Down Home is working to engage voters in our small towns this year to inform them about the upcoming elections, when, where, and how they can vote, and recruit more folks into our movement. Opportunities are available in the following counties: Ashe, Alamance, Cabarrus, Chatham, Franklin, Granville, Iredell, Johnson, Nash, Orange, Person, Pitt, Randolph, Rowan, Rockingham, Vance, Watauga, and Wilson. The ideal candidate is a people-person motivated to build a powerful multiracial base that wins changes for poor and working-class people in rural North Carolina. They have excellent listening skills, are team players and independent workers, and are aligned with Down Home's mission. The Work Have conversations with community members through door-to-door canvassing Participate in 4 to 6 canvasses per week Ensure that data and information collection are consistent and accurate Troubleshooting issues within the program Must be willing to work in a team-centered environment. Required Traits Excellent communication and listening skills: Can engage deeply with people they have just met. Be able to listen to community members and understand their concerns. Can build rapport quickly and is comfortable having relational conversations. Team player: Contribute to a growing and fast-paced team. Take directions well and be willing to offer feedback and suggestions to co-workers and management. Offer support to teammates and ask for help when needed. Independent worker: Be able to complete multiple canvass shifts a week. Meet deadlines and hit metric goals. Ensure that numbers are reported on time with data integrity at the top of mind. Attention to detail and be able to provide thoughtful solutions to problems that arise. Be able to work in a fast-paced environment where work areas are expected to change frequently. Mission alignment: Committed to the vision of a powerful, inclusive, rural, multiracial, working-class movement-building as a path towards liberation for all people. Is aligned with the idea that building power takes both election programs and long-term base-building and community investment. Compensation Compensation for this contract position is $22 hourly. Hours are flexible, with shifts available during the afternoon and evening. This role is not eligible for employee-sponsored benefits or healthcare. Applicants must be able and willing to travel regularly for work. How to Apply Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis if spots are available. We will still accept applications if this job description is posted on Down Home’s website (www.downhomenc.org).
item.dc:creator: Down Home North Carolina

item.title: Support Services Assistant Legislative
item.description: Support Services Assistant-LEGISLATIVE City of Sanibel Sanibel, Florida, United States Full-time 3 days ago $43,222.40 - $63,585.60 USD yearly Description Under general supervision of the City Clerk, is responsible for: meeting and greeting visitors to the City; answering multi-line telephone system; posting City e-mail announcements, Constant Contact and other City social media; developing and processing press releases for web-based posting, social media updates and general public release as directed; and performing assigned clerical and administrative tasks relating to: a. Administering the City’s web-based citizen communications software concerning access to City services and information; or b. Processing and maintaining City-wide contracts and related software, serving as recording secretary for assigned City Committees and Boards, assisting Departments, as required, with the operation and training of employees in the use of Legistar, maintaining office supplies and processing all Department invoices and credit card purchases through the Munis software system. or c. Perform records management functions by creating electronic files and archiving documents. Index and store images according to pre-determined guidelines, ensure scans are precise and adhere to prescribed guidelines. Duties ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned. Meets and greets visitors to the City and answers multi-line telephone system and performs clerical and administrative tasks as assigned. Composes and types general correspondence relating to areas of responsibility. Drafts and posts approved information such as press releases and other information. Writes and/or processes press releases for web-based posting, social media updates and general public release as directed. Provides photographic support as required and performs web-based updates, including include photographs. ALSO PERFORMS DUTIES BELOW, AS ASSIGNED: Remains current on technology changes relating to communications. Performs tasks relating to the City’s web-based citizen communications software concerning access to City services and information. Serves as the citizen communications software help-line administrator for user access to the system as requested by City residents, property owners, contractors and others by for City services and general information. Receives non-emergency requests through the web-based program, maintains a log of requests and follows up to assure completion and final response to the CSS users. Monitors san.council mail on a daily basis for referral the City Manager. Maintains the night ring recording messages. Maintains records and documents for scheduled Committee meetings and prepares final agendas for posting. Prepares and distributes related materials for meetings as needed. Takes, transcribes and types minutes of City Council appointed committee meetings. Refers draft minutes of committee meetings through the City Clerk to the City Manager with recommendations as necessary. Following approval of minutes, maintains official committee file of minutes. Administers the City’s vendor contract process and related software. Serves as the City expert in the Legistar software assisting Departments in the use of Legistar. Responsible for processing all Department invoices and credit card expenditures through the Munis software system. Responsible for ordering supplies for the Legislative and Administration Departments and distributing requisite charges. Responsible for creating electronic files and archiving documents under the City’s records management program. Indexes and stores images according to guidelines ensuring scans are precise and adhere to prescribed benchmarks, thereby eliminating paper copies, reducing use of space, providing ease of access to documents, improve security and accountability of files. Required Education, Experience, License, Registration, and Certification Qualifications QUALIFICATIONS: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE: Associates Degree; supplemented by three (3) years progressively responsible administrative type experience in support services functions such as public relations, communications, journalism, information technology or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Strong writing and excellent computer skills required. Supplemental or Additional Information Ability to read and comprehend complex oral instructions, correspondence and memos. Ability to write press releases, develop brochures and posters Knowledge of computer word processing systems Knowledge of prescribed formats and procedures in preparation of summary minutes Knowledge of indexing and filing systems Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to citizens, contractors, and others who have business with the City. Excellent people skills with the ability to multi-task is essential. Ability to provide quality products, work quickly and with accuracy. Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but generally routine written or oral instructions. Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations. Knowledge and ability to use the City’s software systems. Sanibel, Florida, United States $43,222.40 - $63,585.60 USD yearly

item.title: Campaign Organizer Elect Dan Osborn Flip The Senate
item.description: ampaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin now and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather thousands of support cards from Dan Osborn supporters. Recruit and train volunteers to talk to voters. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Knock on thousands of doors to educate voters about Dan Osborn and his platform. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training, and developing volunteer leaders in your community to talk to their neighbors and community members about Dan Osborn. Completing your own shifts knocking doors to recruit volunteers and have in depth conversations about Dan Osborn for Senate. Engaging and expanding our support network through developing relationships with community leaders. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Summer Associate Internship Public Policy Assistant
item.description: Description The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship program beginning in May 2027 and ending in August 2027. Students will work on impactful projects and meaningful work during their internship. To qualify for this position, applicants must be currently pursuing a degree from an accredited college or university and have an anticipated graduation date of December 2027 or later. As part of Navy Federal's Military Affairs & Strategic Partnerships (MA&SP) department, GRPP collaborates closely with business units across the enterprise to assess policy implications, support strategic decision-making, and represent Navy Federal's interests before policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. The Public Policy Assistant Summer Associate will support the team's policy research, reporting, and operational activities. The associate will help maintain legislative, regulatory, stakeholder engagement, and project-tracking efforts that support the team's advocacy and strategic priorities. Responsibilities may include data analysis, reporting, process improvement, policy research, and the development of materials that help inform decision-making and increase visibility into GRPP activities across the enterprise. This role will provide exposure to public policy, government relations, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration. Potential Projects Include: Support the collection, organization, and analysis of data related to legislative, regulatory, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and project activities. Assist in preparing weekly, monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc reports, executive summaries, briefing materials, and presentations for senior leadership and internal stakeholders. Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations that provide insights into policy developments, advocacy activities, stakeholder engagement, and team performance metrics. Support the tracking and management of team projects, action items, external engagements, and strategic initiatives to improve visibility and operational efficiency. Conduct research on federal and state legislative proposals, regulatory actions, and emerging public policy issues affecting credit unions, financial services, and military-affiliated communities. Perform industry benchmarking and trend analysis to support advocacy priorities and strategic planning efforts. Assist with preparing background materials, stakeholder summaries, and briefing documents for meetings with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and internal business partners. Collaborate with business units across the enterprise to gather information and support policy-related initiatives and reporting. Complete a capstone project focused on improving GRPP's reporting, knowledge management, or operational processes, resulting in recommendations and tools that create long-term value for the team. Responsibilities Support the monitoring and tracking of legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments relevant to Navy Federal and the credit union industry. Conduct research and gather information from legislative, regulatory, industry, and internal sources to support policy analysis and advocacy efforts. Assist with maintaining records of team activities, stakeholder engagements, policy developments, and strategic initiatives. Compile, organize, and analyze data to support team reporting, metrics, and leadership updates. Prepare presentations, briefing materials, summaries, and reports for internal stakeholders and senior leadership. Support project management activities by tracking action items, milestones, and deliverables across multiple initiatives. Collaborate with business units and internal partners to collect information and support cross-functional projects. Help identify opportunities to improve team processes, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Participate in team meetings, stakeholder engagements, and professional development activities to gain exposure to government relations and public policy functions. Qualifications Pursuing a degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, Law, or a related field. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to research, gather, and organize information from a variety of sources. Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Demonstrated interest in public policy, government, financial services, advocacy, or related fields. Desired Qualifications Coursework or project experience in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, or a related field. Experience conducting research, analyzing information, or preparing reports and presentations through coursework, internships, student organizations, or other experiences. Familiarity with data analysis, reporting, data visualization, or business intelligence concepts. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience using Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint to organize information and communicate findings. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries and recommendations. Experience balancing multiple projects, priorities, or extracurricular commitments. Interest in legislative affairs, regulatory issues, government relations, military affairs, consumer financial services, or the credit union industry. Demonstrated leadership through student organizations, volunteer activities, community involvement, athletics, military service, or other experiences. Additional Information Hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM Location: 820 Follin Ln SE, Vienna, VA 22180

item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Description GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES The Public Policy Team works to protect our state’s business climate and regional reputation by supporting key policies at the state and local levels that affect metro Atlanta's economy, talent, and community. The Coordinator role on the Government Affairs team will assist the Public Policy team with legislative tracking, research, administrative tasks, attending and summarizing legislative meetings, monitoring activities at various levels of government, attending and representing the chamber at various meetings, and other tasks as assigned. The Coordinator will report to the Manager of Government Affairs, while collaborating with all Public Policy team members and departments at the chamber. Preferred skills for this role include an understanding of the legislative process and an eagerness for continued growth, the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, strong attention to detail, and the ability to communicate professionally to ensure MAC's success in the public policy sphere. Our ideal candidate is a high-achiever, self-starter, and team player with an interest in deepening their understanding of Georgia’s political landscape and policy skills. Successful candidates will be organized, possess strong networking and communication skills, and demonstrate the ability to manage multiple projects without constant supervision. DAY-TO-DAY DUTIES INCLUDE: Legislative Develop a strong understanding of MAC’s legislative priorities, and work alongside team members to craft strategies and tactics to implement key priorities Monitor, research, and track in real-time legislative activity at the state and local government levels that could impact Georgia and the metro Atlanta region Assist with scheduling and executing meetings with elected officials, executive and legislative staff, business and civic community partners, coalitions, and key stakeholders Manage team-specific documents and resources that are critical to the team's operations and performance at the state capitol Conduct research and prepare policy summaries, briefing forms, talking points, letters of support, etc. Interact wit h federal, state, and local elected officials, department and agency leads, and their staff Assist with coalition building and stakeholder outreach around key legislative priorities Support and assist with the biennial development of the Metro Atlanta Chamber’s policy agenda and legislative priorities Build relationships with key campaign, fundraising, and political staff members Attend outside meetings, conferences, legislative functions, and other job-related events as directed. Administrative Manage accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, and reporting for Metro Atlanta Chamber Political Action Committee (MACPAC) Plan and execute administrative tasks for political entities including accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, ethics reporting, scheduling, communications, etc. Oversee operations of various entities, including fundraising, consultant management and oversight, board communications, ethics reporting, compliance, etc. Coordinate and execute the public policy team's state-mandated ethics reporting Event and Communications Support Assist with planning and execution of chamber events, meetings, initiatives, and other policy events attended by investors, elected officials, staff, and partners. Coordinate and draft internal and external updates on chamber priorities and key legislation Assist with creating department communications, social media, website/blog content, etc. External Foster relationships with MAC members, business community partners, lobbyists, government officials, and government staff Plan and execute meetings with elected officials and staff outside of the metro Atlanta region Perform other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS: One to three years of experience preferred in government affairs, public policy, executive or legislative branch, community affairs, non-profit advocacy, regulatory affairs, or political campaigns Familiarity with the legislative process and Georgia’s political landscape, along with a continued eagerness to grow Ability to quickly synthesize legislation, regulations, data, and strategies, and to communicate them to team members and senior leaders Exceptional attention to detail, organizational skills, and verbal and written communication skills Excellent social and interpersonal skills; capacity to interact with a wide variety of people in government, politics, and civic and business leadership Ability to quickly identify barriers to success and devise strategies or tactics to remove or mitigate them Ability to maintain a non-partisan approach in all respects, work with all members of the executive departments and agencies, and the General Assembly and their staffs Self-starter, capable of working both independently and collaboratively with other team members to produce desired outcomes High energy, versatile, and able to multitask; flexible, able to adapt to changing priorities and plans Qualifications The Metro Atlanta Chamber (MAC) serves as a catalyst for a more prosperous and vibrant metro Atlanta. To advance economic growth and improve our quality of place, MAC is focused on starting, growing, and recruiting companies to our 29-county region. We're also focused on growing our innovation economy by promoting and strengthening connections to drive Atlanta's innovation and entrepreneurial culture. MAC is committed to being an active voice for the business community, serving as an advocate for a competitive business climate, advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion as economic imperatives, and telling Atlanta's story. Our Purpose, Principles, and Core Values MAC's purpose is to UNLEASH ATLANTA'S AMBITION, and in doing so we embody the following principles: Sit Down Together, Stand Up to Act Knock Down Walls, Open Doors Take the Lead, Share the Credit Sharpen the Focus, Expand the Reach At MAC, we naturally exhibit an unwavering commitment to three core values: to be relentless, smart, and all-in . This means every team member is: Relentless . MAC employees take pride in being relentless with an unwavering focus. Our partners trust us to deliver on our commitments. There isn't room for cutting corners, being aimless, or rejecting change. We are bold and persistent and execute with innovation and edge. Smart . Team members at MAC know that intense curiosity allows us to grow. We leverage instinct, integrity, and data to drive our strategy and achieve our purpose. As problem-solving idea generators, we have a natural advantage in any challenge. All-In. We're a greater force when we rally together. It doesn't matter what our title or position is: we trust each other and work as one to multiply our collective impact and achieve ambitious goals.

item.description: Title: Congressional Affairs Specialist Location: Washington, DC 20004 Schedule: Full-time Pay: $160,000-$190,000 annually, commensurate with experience ROLE KMRG, LLC (KMRG) is a federal services company that hires talented professionals to support Government agencies and the communities they serve. We are hiring an experienced Congressional Affairs Specialist to support the Inter-American Foundation (IAF). In this role, you will provide senior-level subject matter expertise supporting congressional and interagency reporting, stakeholder engagement, legislative and appropriations analysis, and executive communications. You will advise and support IAF leadership while Government decisions and approvals remain with IAF. Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Apply today! RESPONSIBILITIES Congressional & Interagency Affairs Serve as a subject matter expert on federal and IAF reporting requirements and U.S. national security alignment Provide technical advice and assistance on IAF engagement with Congress and interagency stakeholders Track and communicate congressional and interagency updates, contacts, emerging issues, and stakeholder interests Monitor laws, legislative history, hearings, OMB circulars, regulations, and controls affecting IAF reporting and oversight Prepare and coordinate congressional RFIs, reports, and related materials for leadership on congressional and interagency matters Draft and edit executive briefings, talking points, memoranda, testimony, Q&A materials, and sensitive communications Coordinate with the Communications Team on external-facing publications and materials Develop an annual external-affairs workplan covering key reports, projects, and engagement milestones Prepare monthly status reports on projects, stakeholders REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS U.S. citizenship Fluency in English and Spanish, oral and written Bachelor’s degree in political science, public administration, public policy, law, international relations, communications, or a related field Minimum 10 years of relevant experience working with Capitol Hill and U.S. executive agencies Strong understanding of legislative and executive branches, including appropriations, budgeting, congressional oversight Experience analyzing legislation, statutory language, and committee reports for operational, legal, or budgetary impacts Experience drafting sensitive executive briefings, testimony, and Q&A materials for congressional or interagency engagements Strong plain-language writing skills and ability to distill complex information into concise executive materials under tight deadlines Experience preparing and clearing responses to Congressional Letters of Inquiry, RFIs, and annual reporting requirements Ability to build effective relationships with cross-agency teams, congressional staff, White House liaisons, and interagency partners Ability to stay current on laws, hearings, OMB guidance, regulations, and controls affecting federal reporting and oversight Strong analytical judgment and the ability to provide timely technical guidance to senior leadership Strong computer skills, including word processing, spreadsheet item.title: Legislative Affairs Coordinator
item.description: BATTERY COUNCIL INTERNATIONAL Legislative Affairs Coordinator Full-time · Washington, DC area required (work from home within the DC area) · Reports to the VP, Government Relations & Sustainability Salary range: $70,000–$90,000, plus bonus and benefits About BCI Battery Council International is the century-old trade association for the North American battery industry. We lead the industry’s federal and state advocacy on recycling, extended producer responsibility, transport, and safety, alongside our technical, data, and sustainability programs. We are a small, remote team, and we are building our state and federal advocacy capability in-house. The role This is the engine room of our advocacy program. You will track what is happening in legislatures across the country, flag what matters, and help BCI act on it. You will also assist with federal matters when state sessions quiet down in the second half of the year. It is a great role for someone early in a government-affairs career who wants real ownership and a national view of policy. What you’ll do Track fifty-state activity — monitor legislation and regulation affecting the battery industry across all states via BCI’s tracking database, and keep a current, reliable picture of what is moving. Watch the federal side — review the Federal Register daily for regulatory actions affecting the industry, follow federal legislation, and keep an eye on industry listservs. Summarize and report — turn developments into concise summaries and tracking reports, and maintain an ongoing issues-management report for the team and members. Write it up — draft articles and updates on policy issues for BCI’s digital publications and website. Support state outreach — help advance BCI’s policy priorities and coordinate with members and allied organizations. Back up federal advocacy — lend a hand on federal work as needed. What you bring A bachelor’s degree in political science, energy, public policy, related field, or equivalent experience. Roughly two to five years of experience in government affairs, legislative tracking, policy research, or a closely related field — strong internship experience considered for early-career candidates. Familiarity with how state (and ideally federal) legislative and regulatory processes work. Sharp research and writing, strong organization, and real attention to detail across a high volume of material. The self-direction to manage a broad workload well on a home-based, distributed team. Nice to have Exposure to environmental, recycling, product-stewardship, or manufacturing policy. Experience with a legislative-tracking platform (Bloomberg Government, Politico, or similar) and with coalition work. What we offer Competitive pay in the range above, plus an annual bonus. A 5% 401(k) match and medical, dental, and vision coverage. Paid time off and a work-from-home schedule based in the DC area, with occasional travel and in-person meetings. A national view of policy and genuine ownership of BCI’s state program, early in your career. Exposure to international policy and global battery-association work. How to apply Submit a resume and cover letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the position is open until filled. Please tell us where in the DC area you are based. Equal opportunity BCI is an equal-opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to an inclusive hiring process and will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities on request at any stage. Contact [email protected] to request accommodations. Battery Council International · batterycouncil.org · The salary range reflects the band for this role; the actual offer depends on experience and work location under BCI’s geographic pay framework.

item.title: Political Science Faculty Member
item.description: $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly About Holyoke Community College: Holyoke Community College is housed on a multi-million-dollar, 135-acre campus, equipped with state-of-the art technology in specialized learning facilities. HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. These are the values which have created a tradition of excellence spanning more than six decades, and which are enabling Holyoke Community College to meet today's challenges. Mission : Educate. Inspire. Connect. Values: Kindness, Inclusion, Trust, Innovation & Collaboration Kindness, inclusion and trust are the foundation of the work that we do together. Innovation and collaboration enable us to explore and implement the ideas that will shape our future. The Critical Social Thought (CST) Department at Holyoke Community College seeks a full-time tenure-track faculty member to bring vision and innovation to Political Science courses within the department’s CST Option. We seek candidates who will bring a broad grounding in US Political Science to the department, and who can enhance our course offerings with specialized areas of expertise. Candidates with research or teaching in US National Politics, State and Local Politics, Civics, Civil Liberties, Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics are particularly encouraged to apply. Our ideal candidate will continue the department’s tradition of interdisciplinary teaching with colleagues across campus and engaging with the external community via community-based learning. As part of the college’s efforts to ensure equitable outcomes for all HCC students, candidates must bring a demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in their teaching practice, as well as a record of excellence in college-level instruction. Primary responsibilities include: teaching lecture classes on general US Political Science topics as well as electives that serve the needs of students in our program as well as other degree programs; strengthening the ongoing development of our CST academic program via assessment and curriculum development; participating in college governance, recruitment and retention efforts; and professional development. In addition to teaching experience, candidates should also demonstrate a commitment to student-centered advising, and to building partnerships that will enhance students’ opportunities for career and transfer. Such partnerships may include internal collaborations with colleagues in the CST department and in the Latinx Studies program as well as external collaborations to expand career and transfer opportunities for students who major in CST and Latinx programs. Although hybrid teaching options may be available, this position will require a substantial amount of in-person, on-campus work with students, faculty, and community partners. Teaching US Political Science lecture courses, in particular general US National as well as State and Local Politics surveys, and courses that address specific subfields in Political Science relevant to the faculty member’s expertise. Ability to teach Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics is of particular interest. Working closely with colleagues in Critical Social Thought Department and across campus, develop innovative teaching methods; expand community-engaged learning initiatives; continue a commitment to innovative, inclusive, discovery-based and critically engaged curricula; incorporate technology in the classroom; develop and implement new courses as appropriate that serve the students’ academic needs, and strengthen the ongoing development of our CST academic program. Advising students in the CST program and related majors. Meeting with and assisting students during regular office hours. Actively participating in department, division, and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance. Maintaining professional expertise in areas of specialization. Participating in college programs and activities. Assisting the Dean, Associate Dean, and Chair of the Critical Social Thought Department to establish and maintain existing academic partnerships with related college programs as well as expand articulation agreements with external college and university programs. Providing college service as required by the MCCC contract, including participation in shared governance committees, sub-committees, or task forces. Minimum Qualifications: Master’s degree in Political Science or closely related field, with the ability to teach standard survey courses (US National, State and Local Government, Civil Liberties) as well as specialized courses within US Political Science and across disciplines; Teaching experience in higher education, specifically as instructor of record; Demonstrated excellent teaching skills including interactive teaching, varied pedagogical strategies, and culturally responsive pedagogies; Experience using instructional technology across teaching modalities (i.e. in physical, hybrid, and online classes) to enable student success; Experience working successfully with a diverse student body, staff, and faculty; Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively on projects and initiatives. Equivalency Statement: We welcome and encourage applicants who do not meet the qualifications as stated above, to put in writing precisely how their background and experience have prepared them for the responsibilities of this position. It is preferred that this document be uploaded separately from the resume, cover letter, and references. Preferred Qualifications: A record of teaching excellence in Political Science at a community college or at the first year/sophomore college level; Ph. D in Political Science or closely related field; Interest in promoting and participating in interdisciplinary learning; Ability to provide leadership within an academic department that will contribute to growth, innovation, and excellence in alignment with institutional goals; Bilingual (English/Spanish). Full-Time, Tenure-Track MCCC/MTA Position: Salary Range: $58,722.00 - $70,786.00. Actual salary will be commensurate with education and experience in accordance with MCCC/MTA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Full State benefits. Funding: State. Start Date: Fall, 2027. Additional Details: Applicants must include a CV, cover letter, and syllabus in one of the following areas: US National Government, State & Local Government, or Civil Liberties. A teaching demonstration is a required part of the interview process. Disability Accommodations: Holyoke Community College is committed to the full inclusion of individuals with disabilities and will ensure the availability of reasonable accommodations. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the Office of People and Talent at (413) 552-2554. Background Check: Employment is contingent upon the successful completion and review of a background check which will include CORI (Criminal Offender Record Information) and SORI (Sex Offender Registry Information). All candidates must have legal authorization to work in the United States. HCC is not sponsoring H1B Visa. Holyoke Community College is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, age, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity or sexual orientation in its programs and activities as required by Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and other applicable statutes and college policies. The College prohibits sexual harassment, including sexual violence. Inquiries or complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, retaliation or sexual violence shall be referred to the College’s Affirmative Action and/or Title IX Coordinator, the Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination, the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission or the United States Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights. Holyoke, Massachusetts, United States $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly

item.title: Vp Government Affairs
item.description: Tinker Federal Credit Union’s Risk department has an immediate opening for a Vice President of Government Affairs! This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the nation’s leading credit unions! We offer competitive pay, a robust benefits package, a “smart casual dress code” and much more! We want you to work and grow at TFCU, so there will be many opportunities for professional development and growth through training and continued education. We value you at TFCU! As a Vice President of Government Affairs, you will be responsible for the following: Manages TFCU’s Government Affairs function and is accountable for developing, recommending, and executing the organization’s legislative, regulatory, and political engagement strategy. Evaluates emerging public policy developments, advises leadership regarding organizational risks and opportunities, and manages the relationships, programs, resources, and external partners necessary to advance TFCU’s approved advocacy priorities. Salary Range: This is an exempt position. The starting salary range is $161,544-$201,930; however, actual placement within the range will be determined individually based on your experience relative to organizational needs and internal salary equity. Schedule: Normally works a weekday schedule, but may be required to work evenings, holidays, or weekends. Required to travel, including overnight travel, with or without advance notice Education/Experience: You must have a bachelor's degree in government, business, public policy, political science, or a related field. At least six years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, lobbying, legislative affairs, regulatory policy, or public policy management is required, including experience managing significant programs, external partners, or cross-functional initiatives. Experience advising senior leadership and representing an organization before elected officials, regulators, or industry associations is required Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Incumbent Bonding REQUIRED by TFCU’s chosen authority. Valid driver’s license, maintaining an acceptable Motor Vehicle Record. Registered federal lobbyist, or ability to register under the Lobbying Disclosure Act within 90 days of hire, is required. Ability and willingness to register as an Oklahoma state lobbyist is also required. Keys to success: In order to be successful as a Vice President of Government Affairs you must possess these qualifications: Ability to translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into concise organizational impact assessments and actionable recommendations. Ability to manage budgets, contracts, consultants, vendors, and multiple concurrent advocacy initiatives. Ability to exercise judgment and represent TFCU’s approved positions within established executive direction and delegated authority. Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and lead cross-functional work without direct reporting authority. Advanced knowledge of lobbying, ethics, disclosure, campaign-finance, PAC, and related compliance requirements. Ability to develop executive and board-level briefings regarding legislative, regulatory, and political developments. Proven ability to develop and maintain strong working relationships with national and state leaders, internal and external stakeholders, and employees at all organizational levels. Ability and willingness to travel for work assignments, including out-of-state travel, which may occur as frequently as quarterly or more often depending on business needs, and to work varied hours as needed. Proficiency in financial services, business, and project management software.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly Position Summary CFR’s Government Affairs operation is focused on actively engaging members of Congress and their staff, executive branch officials, and Washington, DC-based diplomats to provide timely, relevant, and useful analysis to further inform policymaking. Through discussion and examination of the critical challenges facing the United States and the international community, the program seeks to serve as both a direct resource and convener of leading thinkers and practitioners in a nonpartisan forum. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Help craft and set strategy for outreach to members of Congress and congressional staff in innovative and policy relevant ways. Maintain a professional network on Capitol Hill and leverage that network to advance institutional priorities. Moderate and oversee some program events, roundtables, and briefings for policymakers and their staff. Coordinate private consultations for members of Congress and their staff to ensure CFR expertise and products are incorporated into the policymaking process. Develop and implement unique and custom outreach strategies for CFR initiatives and other bespoke institutional priorities. Invite and oversee relationships with outside experts participating in CFR programming. Develop strong working relationships with CFR fellows to promote their expertise and scholarship. Track international affairs developments on Capitol Hill. Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education and Experience 8+ years of related experience, with event planning experience required. Bachelor’s degree in international relations, government, public policy, or other related field is required; master’s degree preferred. Congressional or government relations experience required. Related Skills & Other Requirements Strong judgement, discretion, and strategic instincts to operate in high-level, dynamic, and confidential environment. Established relationships across significant segment of House or Senate environment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including with senior principles. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to multi-task and problem solve independently. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment both independently and on a team. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $145,000 – $155,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers an outstanding benefits package. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly

item.title: Research Associate U S Foreign Policy
item.description: $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly Overview Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR's 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs , the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org. Position Summary CFR’s David Rockefeller Studies Program is one of the country’s largest foreign policy think tanks with a widely respected and influential research staff. The Studies Program’s aim is to advance the discussion of U.S. foreign policy and international affairs through its writing, publications, public outreach, and discussions. As part of the Studies Program, the research associate will support a variety of fellows and programs, including a senior fellow whose work focuses on international relations, foreign policy, and diplomatic history. This role encompasses both administrative and research support, with the balance between the two fluctuating based on fellow and program needs. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC, office on a hybrid basis. CFR defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesday through Thursday considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Provide logistical and administrative support to fellows, including scheduling and calendar management, handling phone calls, and media requests, making travel arrangements, and drafting correspondence Coordinate events, including preparing invitations, making travel arrangements, corresponding with speakers, presiders, and participants, and providing logistical support for the event Conduct research and editing for articles, book chapters, and other publications Assist with budgeting, including tracking monthly income statements, monitoring grant information, potentially drafting grant reports and proposals, creating and updating Excel spreadsheets, and preparing vouchers for reimbursement Assist fellows with social media outreach, including website maintenance and posting and/or using social media platforms, as needed Support other fellows and departments, upon request Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required Minimum Qualifications Experience and Education Bachelor’s degree in a related field such as political science, history, or international relations or other related fields. Demonstrated interest in foreign policy studies, diplomatic history, or related fields Master’s degree preferred, but not required One or more years of related administrative and/or internship experience preferred Related Skills & Other Requirements Excellent research, writing, editing, and communication skills Strong organizational and time management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with others Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and manage sensitive information with discretion. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other digital productivity tools, with strong online research and information-management skills Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $55,000 – $58,000, depending on experience. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations.
