item.title: Student Engagement Specialist School Of Public Policy
item.description: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process . Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants . Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants . This position is funded for 1 year(s); continuation past 1 year(s) will be based on university need, performance, and/or availability of funding. ​ POSITION SPECIFICS ​ The School of Public Policy is seeking a Student Engagement Specialist to lead student engagement initiatives and support student success through community-building, programming, leadership development, career readiness, and student-focused events. The School of Public Policy (SPP) seeks to develop professionals who have the skills to identify, analyze, and solve our major policy issues. Professional development opportunities extend beyond the classroom to career days in Washington, D.C., and Harrisburg, Pennsylvania; the Local Government Expo; policy simulations; and the Next Gen Leadership Academy. The Student Engagement Specialist is at the heart of academic operations for the School’s graduate and undergraduate programs, with experiential learning opportunities, community engagement, and career exploration enhancing student success and career readiness. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Develop and facilitate the School’s Harrisburg and Washington, D.C., career exploration trips Develop and facilitate Next Gen Leadership Academy programming Provide support for the School’s Local Government Initiative Build and maintain relationships with external stakeholders, alumni, and friends of the School Develop and facilitate the School’s fall and spring policy simulation events Participate in SPP leadership meetings, committee meetings, and faculty meetings Attend SPP student and public engagement events Participate in Board of Visitors meetings to discuss student engagement efforts and support strategies to cultivate alumni partnerships Participate in college and university meetings Identify opportunities for the School to strengthen its campus leadership in public service career pathways and education Collaboration skills are vital for this role as the Student Engagement Specialist will also serve a liaison to numerous university partners. This includes the Liberal Arts Career Enrichment Network and Employer Engagement Specialist, Chaiken Center for Student Success, Office of Digital Pedagogies and Initiatives, Alumni Relations and Development, Office of Government and Community Relations, and Penn State Outreach. Important Note : Travel is also required in this role, mainly in the local area (e.g., to government offices, nonprofit organizations, or events with local leaders). Infrequent regional travel (2 to 3 times a year on average) is also expected, including to Washington, D.C., and Harrisburg. Qualifications: Effective written and verbal communication skills Excellent interpersonal skills; inclusive and respectful when working with others Ability to stay organized with a high attention to detail and accuracy while multi-tasking Outstanding problem-solving skills Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 or comparable software used to support communication, recordkeeping, document preparation, and spreadsheet management Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and independently with minimal supervision MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS Bachelor's Degree 1+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted Required Certifications: None Important Application Instructions : Applicants must submit a cover letter addressing their interest and relevant experience, in addition to a resume. Additional Information: The College of the Liberal Arts is supportive of flexible work arrangements when aligned with the ability to meet the needs of the unit and the essential duties of the position. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process. In accordance with College guidelines, this position requires a minimum of three days per week of on-site work at the designated work location. BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies. This position requires that you operate a motor vehicle as a part of your job duties. A valid driver’s license and successful completion of a motor vehicle records check will be required in addition to standard background checks. Penn State does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of a staff employment Visa. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. SALARY & BENEFITS The salary range for this position, including all possible grades, is $44,628.00 - $64,668.00. Salary Structure - Information on Penn State's salary structure Penn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional well-being. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans and substantial paid time off which includes holidays, vacation and sick time. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children. For more detailed information, please visit our Benefits Page . item.description: At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. Job Function: Discovery & Pre-Clinical/Clinical Development Job Sub Function: Biotherapeutics R&D Job Category: Scientific/Technology All Job Posting Locations: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States of America Job Description: At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com . As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. We are searching for the best Senior Scientist, CAR Screening and Lead Selection (CSLS), Cell & Genetic Medicines , based in Cambridge, MA. We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Senior Scientist to join our CAR Screening and Lead Selection team focused on advancing next-generation cell therapies. The Senior Scientist will design, execute, and analyze in vitro assays to characterize and select CAR-T candidates, supporting data-driven decisions that drive pipeline progression across modalities. This role offers the opportunity to work cross-functionally in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with cutting-edge technologies. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong scientific curiosity and a passion for discovery, brings technical expertise across diverse in vitro assays, and is motivated to apply rigorous experimental approaches toward the development of meaningful therapeutics. Key Responsibilities: Contribute to advancing pipeline programs by generating assays and data sets that stratify lead CAR-T candidates. Design, perform, and troubleshoot in vitro assays to evaluate the phenotype and function of CAR-T cell candidates, including cell-based cytotoxicity assays. Thorough analysis and communication of complex data sets, applying results towards determining next-step strategies and troubleshooting. Collaborate closely with colleagues in discovery, process development, and therapeutic area SMEs to align priorities and share data. Contribute to broader team experimental designs, scientific strategy discussions and provide guidance and support to junior team members. Follow best practice lab operations for safety, data integrity, and reproducibility. Maintain clear and accurate records of experimental design, data, and analysis using electronic lab notebook (ELN). Required Qualifications: PhD in immunology, bioengineering, cell biology, or a related field with 2+ years of relevant industry or postdoctoral experience; non-PhDs with 5+ years of experience in biopharmaceutical or biotech working in cell therapy. Hands-on experience and expertise with multiparameter flow cytometry (traditional and/or spectral), including panel design, sample preparation, acquisition, and data analysis. Independent expertise in data analysis and visual representations using GraphPad Prism, Spotfire or similar software. Ability to independently design and execute complex in vitro studies with limited guidance. Self-motivated, highly organized, and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced discovery environment. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to independently drive projects while working collaboratively. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with primary human T cell culture, expansion, and genetic engineering (viral transduction and/or non-viral gene editing). Proficiency in IncuCyte-based assays or comparable real-time cytotoxicity platforms. Experience with intracellular cytokine staining and cytokine arrays, such as MSD or comparable. Demonstrated expertise using ELN systems for experimental documentation, experience with Benchling is a plus. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Work Environment: This is an on-site lab-based role; candidates must be comfortable with extensive bench work and collaborative team science. Why Join Us? Be part of a transformative journey in developing life-saving therapies. Work in a collaborative, innovation-driven environment. Opportunities for growth and professional development. item.title: Government Affairs Spring 2027 Internship
item.description: Government Affairs Spring 2027 Internship Washington, D.C. Ducks Unlimited seeks a motivated college student or recent college graduate to serve in our Washington, DC office as an intern for the Spring 2027 session, to start in January. This person will assist in all facets of carrying out the public policy priorities of this office, including but not limited to assisting with major policy and fundraising events, tracking legislation, attending Congressional hearings and representing Ducks Unlimited at coalition and partner meetings when necessary. Ducks Unlimited is the world's largest nonprofit organization dedicated to conserving North America's continually disappearing waterfowl habitats. Established in 1937, Ducks Unlimited has conserved more than 15 million acres thanks to contributions from more than a million supporters across the continent. Guided by science and dedicated to program efficiency, DU works toward the vision of wetlands sufficient to fill the skies with waterfowl today, tomorrow and forever. This intern will play a critical role in the success of DU’s governmental affairs and policy efforts that directly contribute to achieving the organization’s habitat mission. Candidates must be highly organized and have the ability to manage several tasks at once without requiring extensive supervision. Qualifications: Active college transcript or bachelor’s degree in political science, natural resources, agriculture, or preferred related field, if applicant is a college graduate. Familiarity with or keen interest in learning about congressional and federal regulatory processes. Knowledge of, and interest in wildlife, water resources, waterfowl, agriculture, Ducks Unlimited and/or outdoor recreation-related conservation issues. Practice in critical thinking and willingness to learn. Experience with Microsoft Suite. Responsibilities: Manage and assist with the logistics related to DU events held in DC, including advocacy fly-ins, Capitol Hill banquets and other receptions and events. Support the governmental affairs team with scheduling Congressional and Administration meetings, conducting policy research, and providing general support for all public policy activities. Assist in the daily administration and organization of the DC governmental affairs office. Assist the team in developing internal and external communications such as press releases. Provide administrative and logistical support for internal and external meetings, materials preparation and tasks related to meeting follow-up. Provide staff support to DU’s volunteer Public Policy Committee. Support governmental affairs team lobbying efforts through developing, implementing and tracking policy-related information. Other office duties as assigned. Required to Submit: Resume Cover letter expressing your interest and qualifications for the position. This role is a Seasonal Internship and does not offer benefits or 401K. DUCKS UNLIMITED, INC. item.title: Legislative Analyst
item.description: General Summary This is work functioning as a technical expert to the Office of the Minority Leader, legislators, and the public on the subject matter under the jurisdiction of this office. Under close supervision of a staff director and Minority Leader, the legislative analyst applies this expertise when researching and preparing proposed budgets, staff analyses, reports, substantive legislation, responding to inquiries, and developing correspondence. Financial Disclosure: Pursuant to sections 112.3144 and 112.3145, F.S., this position is required to electronically file a Form 1 – Statement of Financial Interests with the Florida Commission on Ethics within 30 days of hire. Examples of Work Performed Analyzes and objectively summarizes proposed legislation to determine its effectiveness and the impact of its passage on the state and other entities and individuals. Researches and drafts legislation and amendments to legislation at the direction of the staff director or leadership team. Assists in planning briefings to include agenda, speakers, presentations, and materials. Monitors the implementation of legislation in the Executive and Judicial Branches to ascertain that legislative intent is met. Briefs legislators verbally or in writing on issues to be discussed in committee, on the floor, or with constituents. Conceives, plans, and conducts research projects. Prepares oral and written reports on research and other work such as end of session reports, interim projects, and oversight reports which include recommendations for legislative action. Provides information and problem-solving assistance to legislators, their constituents, and the public. Prepares letters, summaries, talk-sheets or speeches, reports, and informational memoranda on issues at the request of the leadership team or staff director. Keeps abreast of new and ongoing issues affecting assigned area of responsibility by collecting resource materials, attending workshops and conferences, reading industry publications, communicating with agency personnel, and the public. Assists in the coordination of the work of the administrative assistant, legislative intern, and other staff members. Serves as liaison with state agencies. May operate a computer to perform word processing, database management, and/or spreadsheet applications. Performs other related duties as required. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Knowledge of state budgeting processes and structure. Knowledge of legal terminology and legal research. Knowledge of committee subject area: commerce, budget and business regulation. Knowledge of applicable computer, spreadsheet, databases, and word processing programs. Knowledge of Florida state government, legislative rules, and procedures. Skill in reading comprehension, analysis, and organization. Ability to communicate effectively and concisely, both orally and in writing. Ability to take action in situations which lack clear direction. Ability to take initiative on independent research projects. Ability to produce quality work under pressure. Ability to deal tactfully and courteously with the demands of members, their staff, the public, press, and lobbyists. Ability to plan, organize, and coordinate work assignments. Ability to work cooperatively as a team member and to contribute to the efficient internal functioning of the committee staff. Ability to conduct in-depth, carefully documented and credible analysis under minimal supervision within established deadlines. Ability to conduct meetings and to make presentations. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with others. Ability to work independently. Ability to collect and analyze data. Ability to organize data into logical format for presentation in reports, documents, and other written materials. Ability to solve problems and make decisions. Ability to exercise discretion and confidentiality. Minimum Qualifications A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and three years of professional experience in research, analysis, program planning and evaluation, or administrative work. A master's degree from an accredited college or university can substitute for one year of the required experience. A doctorate from an accredited college or university can substitute for two years of the required experience. Professional experience as described above may substitute on a year-for-year basis for the required college education. Base Salary: Commensurate with experience. The Legislature offers a competitive benefits package. Submission of Application: Interested parties may send a cover letter, resume and completed Florida Legislature Employment Application via GovernmentJobs.com or send an Alternate Application (PDF) to: Office of Administration & Professional Development Florida House of Representatives 402 South Monroe Street, 1201 Capitol Tallahassee, Florida 32399 Or email HouseAPD@FLHouse.gov Accommodation for Disability: If an accommodation is needed for a disability, please notify Human Resources at (850) 488-6803.

item.title: Senior Federal Lobbyist
item.description: American Association of University Professors Political Department Senior Federal Lobbyist – Hybrid position based in Washington, D.C. The American Association of University Professors (AAUP), a fast-growing union of higher education workers, is pleased to announce a professional position for a Senior Federal Lobbyist, to be filled as soon as possible. Our goals are to build AAUP member power in order to defend the higher ed sector against increasing attacks and lead a fight for fair wages, job security, academic freedom, an end to student debt, and expanded access to postsecondary education. The Senior Federal Lobbyist leads the American Association of University Professors' (AAUP), an affiliate of the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), AFL-CIO, federal advocacy agenda, serving as the primary liaison to Capitol Hill, executive agencies, and national advocacy coalitions. Reporting directly to the Political Director, this person will develop and execute legislative and regulatory initiatives to champion higher education as a public good, safeguard academic freedom, protect shared governance and faculty tenure, advance labor and collective bargaining rights, and secure robust federal funding for higher education and scientific research. The ideal candidate combines sharp political acumen with exceptional attention to detail, innovative out-of-the-box thinking, and outstanding interpersonal skills. As a key team player within the Political & Legislative Affairs department, the lobbyist will collaborate across teams and affiliate organizations to translate complex policy into high-impact advocacy strategies. The AAUP is committed to a diverse workforce and strives to achieve a workplace environment respectful of the many cultures of our own employees and the higher education workers we represent, including a significant number of African-American, Asian-American/Pacific Islander, and Latinx employees, as well as LGBTQl-identified employees, and those who have immigrated from various countries. The AAUP values the benefits that diversity brings to the faculty profession and the labor movement. We seek applicants whose experience and perspective will contribute to strong representation of our diverse members. Duties and Responsibilities The position will include the following responsibilities: Federal Advocacy & Legislative Strategy Capitol Hill Engagement: Serve as the principal registered lobbyist for the AAUP before Congress, maintaining active, collaborative, and bipartisan relationships with key committees (e.g., Senate HELP, House Education & the Workforce, Appropriations) and leadership offices. Executive Branch & Agency Liaison: Monitor and influence federal rulemaking and regulatory policy within the U.S. Department of Education, National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), Department of Labor (DOL), NSF, NIH, and the White House. Policy Monitoring & Analysis: Rigorously track federal legislation, executive orders, and agency guidance. Perform thorough, detailed policy analyses on issue areas affecting higher education, academic freedom, civil rights, labor rights, and research funding. Creative Strategy: Bring innovative, out-of-the-box strategies to legislative campaign planning, identifying non-traditional avenues and message framing to advance AAUP priorities in challenging political environments. Policy Writing & Precision Communications Detail-Oriented Deliverables: Draft and meticulously edit high-priority advocacy materials, including legislative briefs, congressional testimony, sign-on letters, administrative comments, and background memos for AAUP leadership where accuracy and precision are paramount. Member Updates: Translate complex legislative developments into clear, accessible, and actionable updates for AAUP state conferences, campus chapters, and national membership. Coalition Leadership & Collaborative Partnerships Coalition Engagement: Represent the AAUP in national coalitions alongside higher education associations, labor unions (such as our affiliate, the AFT), civil rights groups, and scientific advocacy networks. Joint Campaigns: Build strong consensus and lead collaborative campaigns on shared federal priorities, including Title IV/Pell Grants, student loan reform, research funding, and defending public higher education against political interference. Member Mobilization, Event Coordination & Internal Collaboration Annual Capitol Hill Fly-In & Lobby Day: With the assistance of cross-departmental staff and legislative team members, lead the strategic planning, messaging, precision scheduling, and execution of AAUP's annual fly-in and lobby day on Capitol Hill. Team-Oriented Integration: Serve as a proactive team player within the Political & Legislative Affairs department, working closely with the Political Director, state policy leadership, and grassroots team to align federal policy goals with member mobilization. Ethics & Compliance: Meticulously maintain compliance records to ensure 100% adherence to the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA), federal ethics rules, and required reporting standards. Qualifications Professional Experience: 5–10 years of progressive experience in federal government relations, congressional staff roles (e.g., Legislative Director, Senior Committee Staff, Counsel), higher education policy, or labor advocacy. Uncompromising Attention to Detail: Exceptional precision in policy analysis, statutory language review, advocacy writing, compliance reporting, and event schedule management. Interpersonal Excellence & Teamwork: Proven track record as a collaborative team player with strong relationship-building skills across diverse political, labor, academic, and coalition stakeholders. Innovative Problem Solving: Ability to think out of the box to navigate complex legislative landscapes, craft compelling narratives, and develop creative advocacy tactics. Legislative & Budget Expertise: Deep working knowledge of federal legislative processes, statutory reauthorizations (e.g., Higher Education Act), federal budget/appropriations cycles, and administrative rulemaking. Event Leadership: Proven capability to coordinate and run large-scale advocacy events, fly-ins, or member lobbying days on Capitol Hill with high organizational precision. Mission Alignment: Deep commitment to the principles of academic freedom, shared governance, tenure, equity and civil rights in education, and collective bargaining rights. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Law, or related field required; Master’s, J.D., or Ph.D. preferred. This job description is not designed or intended to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Activities, duties, and responsibilities may change, or new ones may be assigned during the course of employment.

item.description: At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers. When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the microphone and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 6,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing. Director, Public Policy Why We Have This Role As the Director of Policy, you will serve as the primary expert monitoring, interpreting, and responding to the evolving healthcare policy landscape. You will lead strategic efforts to identify regulatory trends, analyze reporting requirements (including CAHPS, quality, safety, and value-based payment models), and evaluate their impact on product strategy and client operations. Serving as the company liaison to key government and industry bodies—such as CMS, NQF, and AHRQ—you will develop corporate positions, draft public comment letters, and advocate on behalf of Press Ganey and our healthcare clients. If you are a high-level policy expert with executive presence and a passion for shaping healthcare strategy, this role offers significant influence. How You’ll Find Success Regulatory Landscape Mastery: Expertly analyzes and interprets developments in CAHPS, quality reporting, and value-based payment programs to inform executive strategy. Strategic Stakeholder Advocacy: Establishes and nurtures key relationships with CMS, NQF, AHRQ, and health policy stakeholder groups to advocate for business and client interests. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partners closely with Product Management, Sales, Marketing, and Operations to signal strategic opportunities and guide product enhancements. Executive Communication & Thought Leadership: Delivers high-impact policy updates to C-suite client executives and represents the company as a key speaker at industry events. Policy Team Leadership: Directs, coaches, and manages the public policy team while overseeing annual department budgeting and strategic goal alignment. How You’ll Grow Drive company-wide strategy at the intersection of healthcare technology, regulatory compliance, and public policy. Elevate your professional standing as a prominent health policy thought leader across national conferences, client summits, and industry panels. Deepen direct working relationships with federal policy officials and key regulatory governing bodies. Scale and mentor a high-performing public policy research and regulatory data team. Things You’ll Do Monitor & Interpret Policy: Track developments across the health policy landscape to inform product, marketing, and operational strategy. Lead Government Liaisons: Act as the primary organizational liaison to CMS, NQF, AHRQ, and related governmental or public policy entities. Develop Corporate Positions: Draft, review, and submit official comment letters and position statements for rulemaking and requests for information (RFIs). Author & Present Policy Content: Produce regulatory updates for clients and present policy trends at client meetings and industry events. Direct Public Policy Team: Manage Policy Analysts and Senior Regulatory Data Analysts, guiding research projects, annual performance goals, and department budgets. What We’re Looking For On Your Resume 10+ years of experience in the health policy arena, regulatory affairs, or a related healthcare industry role. Demonstrated experience developing corporate position statements and drafting official comment letters for rulemaking. Bachelor’s Degree in Health Policy, Public Health, Business, or related field required (Master’s Degree preferred). Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with proven executive presence. Ability to navigate a matrixed corporate environment and lead direct reports effectively. What You Should Know About This Team Strategic Core: We sit within Product Management and Enterprise Strategy to directly influence our product vision and business roadmap. Advocacy & Impact: We proactively represent healthcare organizations to safeguard business interests and advance quality reporting standards. Thought Leadership Focus: We serve as the trusted regulatory voice for both internal leadership teams and external health system leaders. Travel Expectation: This role involves approximately 25% travel for client meetings, regulatory sessions, and industry events. Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits Comprehensive Health & Wellness Coverage: Industry-leading medical, dental, and vision packages for employees and dependents. Executive Leadership Development: Opportunities for high-visibility leadership, professional association involvement, and career growth. Generous Paid Time Off: Comprehensive paid vacation, sick leave, and paid company holiday schedule. 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan: Competitive company matching contributions to support your long-term financial health. The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life . #hybrid Qualtrics is an equal opportunity employer meaning that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic. ​​​​​​​Applicants in the United States of America have rights under Federal Employment Laws: Family & Medical Leave Act , Equal Opportunity Employment , Employee Polygraph Protection Act Qualtrics is committed to the inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Qualtrics will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please let your Qualtrics contact/recruiter know. No spam - we promise! You'll hear from us two times a month max with fresh, totally tailored info - so be sure to stay connected as you explore your best role and company fit. item.title: Cybersecurity Technical Project Manager Us Senate
item.description: EnDyna is seeking a cybersecurity professional with project-management experience to lead technical delivery and coordinate a multidisciplinary team for anticipated support to the U.S. Senate Office of the Sergeant at Arms. This role combines cybersecurity judgment, organized program execution and clear communication with government stakeholders. Experience supporting Congress or other legislative-branch organizations is strongly preferred. The successful candidate will translate security needs into practical work plans, guide technical specialists, track risks and deliverables, and help protect sensitive systems while maintaining mission continuity. We are especially interested in candidates who understand the Senate’s operating environment, stakeholder relationships, decision-making processes and service expectations. Responsibilities Lead cybersecurity work planning, task execution and delivery, including schedules, staffing coordination, dependencies, risks, quality reviews and status reporting. Serve as a primary coordination point for government stakeholders, technical teams and specialist partners; communicate issues, options and decisions clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Coordinate work across vulnerability management, security assessments, threat intelligence, security operations, incident response and cybersecurity engineering. Guide implementation and improvement of security architecture, risk-management practices and controls, drawing on frameworks such as NIST CSF, RMF and Zero Trust as applicable to the customer’s environment. Track findings from assessments and independent penetration testing through prioritization, remediation coordination and verification; preserve clear ownership and evidence of completion. Help integrate cybersecurity workflows with enterprise tools, including ServiceNow and security monitoring, endpoint detection and response, and incident-management platforms. Develop and review work plans, technical reports, procedures, briefings, performance measures and executive-level updates. Coordinate requirements across system owners and service providers, protecting sensitive information and minimizing disruption to legislative operations. Coordinate compliance reviews, supply-chain risk activities, training and knowledge transfer with the appropriate specialists; maintain clear ownership across the delivery team. Required Qualifications A minimum Secret security clearance, maintained throughout performance; certain tasks may require a higher clearance. Final requirements are subject to the solicitation and customer approval. Demonstrated experience leading cybersecurity projects or technical workstreams, including planning, stakeholder coordination, delivery oversight and issue resolution. Substantive cybersecurity experience sufficient to evaluate technical findings, guide specialists and communicate risk and recommended action. Working knowledge of vulnerability management, security operations, incident response, security architecture and risk-management practices. Experience producing clear technical documentation, management reports and presentations for government or similarly sensitive organizations. Ability to coordinate multiple priorities and technical contributors while maintaining accountability for schedules, quality and follow-through. Strong written and verbal communication, sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive operational information. Preferred Qualifications Direct experience supporting the U.S. Senate, U.S. House of Representatives or another legislative-branch organization. Knowledge of Congressional IT operations, governance, stakeholder coordination, decision processes and the practical requirements of supporting legislative functions. Experience leading teams in an environment with sensitive systems, demanding service expectations and multiple organizational stakeholders. Familiarity with ServiceNow cybersecurity workflows and integration with security monitoring, EDR, SIEM/SOAR or incident-management tools. Experience coordinating independent penetration-testing services, threat hunting, digital forensics or supply-chain security work. Relevant project-management or cybersecurity certifications, such as PMP, CISSP or CISM. Opportunity Details This opportunity is contingent upon contract award and client approval. Final responsibilities, work arrangements and start date will be aligned with the awarded scope and customer requirements. To Apply Please submit your resume highlighting cybersecurity delivery leadership, relevant technical responsibilities, government customers supported and any Congressional or legislative-branch experience. Include relevant professional certifications and your current security-clearance level. Do not include classified or sensitive project information.

item.title: Government Affairs Specialist Gs 0343 14 Nf
item.description: Summary This Government Affairs Specialist is located in Office of Legislative and Public Affairs (OLPA). The primary purpose of the position is responsible for assisting in the development of OLPA's legislative strategy and assisting the Branch Chief for Government Affairs in executing that strategy. Duties As a Government Affairs Specialist , you will perform the following duties: Assists the Branch Chief for Government Affairs in formulating and executing the legislative strategy; conducts research and develops various agency-wide products, such as testimony, talking points, roll out plans and briefing memos. Develops and implements outreach strategies to a variety of communities, including the development of strategic outreach tools and products that cross-cut OLPA. Plans and organizes legislative-related briefings and meetings, handling or assigning administrative details, and oversees preparation of final reports, products, and presentations. Manages and coordinates special events and projects that cross-cut OLPA and NSF, including briefings for Congressional staff. Manages OLPA's automatic notification of awards for Congress in conjunction with appropriate divisions in NSF. Plans work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules for completion of work approximately 20% of the time.. Requirements Conditions of employment You must be a U.S. citizen. Selectee will be required to have a background investigation prior to onboarding. Selectee may be required to serve a 1-year probationary period. Additional Requirements: Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade/equivalent. You must meet eligibility and qualification requirements within 30 days of the closing date. You must answer all job-related questions in the NSF eRecruit questionnaire and any external assessment that is included. All online applicants must provide a valid email address. If your email address is inaccurate or your mailbox is full/blocked, you may not receive important communication that could affect your consideration for this position. It is NSF policy that personnel employed at, or Intergovernmental Personnel Act (IPA) individuals detailed to, NSF are not permitted to participate in foreign talent recruitment programs . Failure to comply with this NSF policy could result in disciplinary action up to and including removal from Federal Service or termination of an IPA assignment and referral to the Office of Inspector General. NSF has determined that all of its positions are eligible for situational telework. Situational telework may be approved on an occasional basis in accordance with agency policy, supervisory approval, and operational requirements. Selected candidates interested in telework, or other workplace flexibility arrangements, should discuss available options with the selecting official. Participation in telework is voluntary and requires an approved telework agreement. Qualifications To qualify at the GS-14 level , you must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 Levelproviding technical leadership managing a legislative or government affairs program, advising executive officials on organizational decisions, and designing innovative strategies to achieve complex short- and long-term goals. Examples include: Led the planning, coordination, and execution of legislative or government affairs programs, ensuring alignment with agency priorities, statutory requirements, and strategic objectives. Directed the review and analysis of proposed legislation, congressional inquiries, and policy initiatives to assess potential impacts on agency operations, programs, and resources. Prepared executive-level briefings, decision memoranda, talking points, and recommendations to support informed decisions on complex legislative and policy matters. Experience refers to paid/unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training/experience that translates directly to paid work. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Education Education may enhance skills required for this position; however, no substitution of education for specialized experience may be made at this level. Additional information Relocation expenses WILL NOT be paid. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP) ICTAP and Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provide eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP or CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP or CTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well-qualified you must meet the following: OPM qualification requirements for the position, all selective factors, where applicable; special OPM approved qualifying conditions for the position; is physically qualified with reasonable accommodation, where appropriate, to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position upon entry; and receives a rating of at least "Very Good" on the assessment. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP or CTAP eligibility, or a copy of your separation personnel action form. Additional information regarding ICTAP or CTAP eligibility is available from OPM's Career Transition Resources . Veterans' Preference: If you are entitled to veterans' preference, you should indicate the type of veterans' preference you are claiming on your resume. Your veterans' preference entitlement will be verified by the employing agency. For 5-point veterans' preference, please provide your DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty), official statement of service from your command if you are currently on active duty, or other official documentation (e.g., documentation of receipt of a campaign badge or expeditionary medal) that proves your military service was performed under honorable conditions. For 10-point veterans' preference, please submit a SF-15 (Application for 10-Point Veteran Preference), DD-214, and official documentation of a compensable service-connected disability of 10% or more or other required documentation as specified on the SF-15. Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request a RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you received the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need a RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments . item.title: Assistant Associate Professor Comparative Political Science
item.description: Current Employees: If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet . The Department of Political Science in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Miami seeks applicants for a tenure-track/tenure-eligible faculty appointment in Political Science. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor and will begin August 15, 2027. We seek a political scientist whose research focuses on comparative politics. We welcome applications from scholars studying any substantive area within comparative politics. The successful candidate will strengthen and expand the department's comparative politics curriculum while supporting existing instructional needs, including routine teaching of our introductory comparative politics course. We are especially interested in candidates with strong methodological training who can contribute to the department's offerings in research methods and data analysis and, where appropriate, to the University's popular Law and Politics minor. We seek faculty of exceptional promise or established national prominence whose scholarship will enrich and expand the department's research profile and educational curriculum. Successful candidates will maintain an active and visible research agenda, contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring, and participate fully in the intellectual life of the department, College, and University. The successful candidate will help increase the College's research capacity, expand existing strengths in global and comparative political research, and contribute to building a nationally and internationally recognized area of excellence. The position offers opportunities to leverage existing faculty networks and partnerships while creating new avenues for interdisciplinary collaboration and scholarly visibility. The University of Miami provides exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary and international engagement. The successful candidate may find opportunities for collaboration across the College and University, including with faculty in the School of Law and other units. Candidates interested in international and experiential learning may also contribute to existing study abroad programs and develop new opportunities for student engagement abroad. Minimum qualifications include a Ph.D. in Political Science by the start date of the appointment. Interested applicants must apply online through the University’s Careers Website . Applicants should compile the following into a single PDF document and upload it under the CV/Resume link: cover letter, CV, research statement, and a teaching statement focusing on your ability to contribute to the undergraduate political science / public administration majors through teaching and mentoring activities. Please arrange for three reference letters to be sent directly to the search chair at umpolsearch@miami.edu. Applications received on or before November 30, 2026, will be given full consideration, though the committee will continue to accept applications until the position is filled. For further information about the position please contact Dr. Casey Klofstad, Chair, umpolsearch@miami.edu . Additional information about the department is available at http://www.as.miami.edu/politicalscience/ . The University of Miami is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants and employees are protected from discrimination based on certain categories protected by Federal law. Job Status: Full time Employee Type: Faculty

item.description: - Director, Federal Government Affairs PMI US, the maker of ZYN and IQOS, Washington, D.C., US PMI US’s Federal Government Affairs team is seeking a Director of Federal Government Affairs in Washington, D.C. We’re looking for an entrepreneurial, intellectually curious and results-driven professional who demonstrates initiative, creativity and a strong work ethic. Reporting to the Head of Federal Government Affairs, you will collaborate with the U.S. External Affairs team and global colleagues to advance the company’s policy agenda. Your day to day: Develop and maintain relationships with Members of Congress and staff, Executive Branch agencies and officials, and other key stakeholders. Develop and lead advocacy campaigns supporting domestic policy objectives. Serve as an in-house specialist on the U.S. Senate, advising management on policy risks, opportunities and strategies. Provide legislative analysis and develop policy statements, position papers, letters and legislative summaries. Lead legislative efforts in Congress, particularly the Senate, to advance health policy dialogue surrounding tobacco harm reduction. Who we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 10–15 years of experience within the Federal Government, Capitol Hill, private sector, business associations, think tanks or public interest organizations. Professional experience in health care policy. Strong bipartisan relationships and ability to work across the political spectrum. Excellent interpersonal, networking, strategic-thinking and communication skills. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. Preferred Qualifications: Experience and relationships with congressional leadership and/or Senate HELP, Finance or Appropriations committees. Demonstrated leadership and a track record of legislative success. Ability to succeed in a fast-paced team environment while working independently. Annual Base Salary Range: $202,400–$253,000 What we offer: Competitive base salary and annual bonus based on position level. Medical, dental and vision coverage. 401(k) with company match. Wellness and commuter benefits, pet insurance and generous PTO. Smart Work, our hybrid working model. An inclusive, diverse culture with opportunities to develop your skills and career within a global business. The opportunity to contribute to our smoke-free future. PMI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. For more information, visit PMI US and PMI Science.

item.description: Community Canvassers and Team Leaders Hiring Immediately - $25-$26/hr + bonuses Full-time & Part-time It’s your time to step up for Nebraska and get out the vote! We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. We are looking for Canvassers to build support in the community for Dan Osborn for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team. Get paid well! Canvassing positions start at $25/hour. Paid training at $20/hr for first 3 days.Team Lead positions start at $26/hour. We offer overtime pay, and multiple bonuses for working full-time or referring your friends. Apply here: https://www.theoutreachteam.net/interest-form-tot Locations: Anywhere in Nebraska - Our main offices are in Omaha, Lincoln, and Grand Island but we are looking for folks to work anywhere in the state We are hiring immediately, all positions run through 11/3/26 with possibilities for advancement afterwards. Standard Shifts run from 11:45am - 8pm weekdays and weekends with the possibility to work part-time or full-time, we also have flexible schedules available Canvasser Responsibilities ($25/hr): Paid training at $20/hr for first 3 days Engage with the public in a friendly and respectful manner Deliver a compelling campaign message, and collect complete survey answers from voters Participate in staff training to improve outreach skills Follow the campaign's safety protocols Team Leader Responsibilities ($26/hr): The Canvasser Responsibilities plus: Manage a small group of canvassers out in the field by checking in with them periodically throughout the day, and debriefing with them at the end of the day Ensure each canvasser has all of the materials they need to be successful Assist directors with canvasser training and administrative work The ideal candidate: Passionate about progressive politics and fostering democracy Strong communication skills; you should enjoy working with other people and be willing and excited to speak with everyone Hard worker who will stay motivated to engage as many people as possible Open to new challenges and are interested in building their campaign skills Culturally competent and able to respectfully engage with teammates and the community Prior canvassing experience is preferred, but not required. Apply here: https://www.theoutreachteam.net/interest-form-tot We are committed to equity, inclusion, and anti-racism. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. Note: Employees must be eligible to work in the US. Upon hire, everyone will be required to present original, and unexpired documents from the Lists of Acceptable Documents to complete the I-9 form verification.

item.title: Sr Coordinator Public Policy And Corporate Strategy
item.description: NeighborWorks as a Company and an Employer For nearly 50 years, Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation, a congressionally chartered national nonprofit known as NeighborWorks® America, has strived to make every community safer and more prosperous. Our network of excellence includes nearly 250 nonprofits in every state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and on Native lands. NeighborWorks offers grant funding, peer exchange, technical assistance, evaluation tools, and access to best-in-class training as the nation’s leading trainer of housing and community development professionals. NeighborWorks network organizations build homes and apartments, expanding the supply of affordable housing in every community; provide financial counseling and coaching that increases self-sufficiency; encourage resident leadership; and collaborate with local stakeholders in the areas of health, economic development, employment, and education. Caring for communities starts with caring for our internal community, our staff. Picture yourself in a collaborative and diverse hybrid environment surrounded by colleagues who challenge, encourage and inspire you. This opportunity offers an impressive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match of up to 12%, 11 paid holidays, generous leave (including 40 hours of paid volunteer time) and industry-leading benefits. Start your career with NeighborWorks America and take advantage of our Staff Training and Education Program (STEP), designed to support continued learning and professional development. Our benefits are designed to support staff holistically, enabling them to give their best in both work and life. We are a mission-based organization committed to building a high-performing work culture, guided by the following core values: We hold ourselves and each other accountable. We act with integrity. We lead with curiosity. We pursue excellence with courage. We respect, honor and celebrate each other. We collaborate with purpose. Work at a Glance: Coordinating Strategy, Operations, and Engagement. Position Summary: Provides comprehensive operational, administrative, project management, budget, communications, and strategic support to the Public Policy and Legislative Affairs (PPLA) and Corporate Strategy & Impact (CSI) divisions. The position serves as a key shared resource supporting the Senior Vice Presidents of both divisions and coordinating activities that advance divisional and organizational objectives. Responsibilities include meeting and event management, communications and content management, stakeholder engagement, project coordination, budget administration, planning and reporting and day-to-day operational support. The incumbent works independently to manage multiple priorities, facilitate cross-functional collaboration, and ensure efficient and effective operations across both divisions. Essential Duties/Responsibilities: This position provides dedicated support to both the PPLA and CSI divisions. The incumbent is expected to balance priorities across both divisions, work collaboratively with the respective Senior Vice Presidents and staff, and serve as a liaison with internal and external stakeholders to support division and enterprise-wide initiative: Strategic Planning, Reporting, and Performance Management Support the development, implementation, and monitoring of division goals, scorecards, work plans, and performance metrics. Track progress against strategic objectives and prepare periodic performance updates. Coordinate and prepare reports, presentations, correspondence, and other materials for executive leadership and external stakeholders. Assist in the development of reports, submissions, and documentation required by senior leadership, board committees, government entities, or other external partners. Meeting and Event Planning Coordinate and support the planning and execution of in-person, virtual, and hybrid meetings, conferences, advisory council meetings, training events, and special initiatives. Manage meeting logistics, agendas, materials, participant communications, and follow-up actions. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure successful event execution. Support team engagement activities, meeting facilitation, and other organizational events as needed. Communications and Content Management Serve as content coordinator and administrator for divisional intranet, website, and other communication platforms. Ensure divisional information, documents, and resources remain current and accurate. Develop, review, and update internal and external communications, presentations, correspondence, and informational materials. Support document management, retention practices, and information governance initiatives. Stakeholder Relations and Special Initiatives Coordinate activities involving internal and external stakeholders, including network organizations, advisory groups, government agencies, congressional staff, industry partners, and other constituent groups as applicable. Facilitate outreach efforts and collaborative projects across divisions and partner organizations. Provide support for special initiatives, strategic projects, and executive-level priorities. Budget Administration and Financial Management Serve as the division Budget Manager and oversee budget-related activities. Manage the division purchase card (P-card) program and monitor expenditures. Establish and maintain divisional budgets within NetSuite. Track budget performance and prepare budget reports in collaboration with division leadership. Assist with budget planning, forecasting, and other financial management activities as required. Division Operations and Administration Ensure smooth division operations and facilitate effective cross-functional collaboration. Support compliance with organizational requirements and deadlines, including timesheets, performance management activities, training requirements, scorecards, and routine corporate reporting. Serve as a division liaison for organization-wide operational initiatives, technology implementations, and process improvements. Collaborate with internal stakeholders to resolve operational, administrative, and technical issues. Administrative Support Provide administrative and operational support to the Senior Vice Presidents and staff in the divisions. Coordinate calendars, meetings, travel arrangements, subscriptions, memberships, and office resource needs. Prepare correspondence, presentation materials, and meeting documentation. Perform other duties and special projects as assigned. Nature of Work Contacts: NeighborWorks staff, field operations and managers of other divisions to coordinate activities, exchange information for reports and provide directives on behalf of the SVP Staff of NeighborWorks organizations, Congressional staffers, staff of federal agencies and vendors. Fiscal Responsibilities: Delegated authority to utilize divisions' purchase card. Processing expenses. Acting as each Division's Budget manager. Required Minimum Qualifications: (a) Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Communications, Management, Organizational Leadership, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience. (b) Experience: Three (3) to five (5) years progressively responsible experience in operations management, executive administration, project coordination, budget administration, office management, or a related function. Must have experience supporting senior leaders and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. (c) Licenses, Certifications: None specified (d) Competencies, Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe. Must demonstrate skills in developing reports, presentations, communications, and other materials for management and executive audiences. Demonstrated competencies in managing budgets, monitoring expenditures, and maintaining financial records. Strong organizational and problem-solving skills and comfort with taking initiative. Excellent interpersonal communications. Collaborative, team-oriented. Highly adaptable, flexible, and able to function well with complex systems and processes. Attention to detail. Strong writing and editing skills. Confidentiality and discretion at high level are required with experience and understanding of the needs and requirements of supporting multiple teams (e) NeighborWorks America Staff are expected to demonstrate excellence in the following : Sensitivity to racial, gender, sexual orientation and cultural differences Effective, respectful, and timely communications with internal and external stakeholders Listening effectively, seeks and accepts feedback Analytic, thoughtful and strategic thinking Considering the mission, objectives, and goals of NeighborWorks and demonstrating an understanding of the impact of her/his/their decisions and behavior on the organization (f) Technology: Microsoft Office Suite; knowledge of or comfort with learning specialized technology systems to support administrative and budget functions, such as NetSuite, Prism, PeopleSoft, etc. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with project management principles or work towards a PMP certificate also a plus. Working Conditions: (a) Travel: up to 5% (b) Physical/Sensory Demands: High demand, very busy environment with little down time (c) Hybrid : This role reports into the office 2 days per week. Salary Range: $80,000- $91,000 The salary offered for the role will be based on a variety of factors, including geographic location, internal equity, and the candidate’s qualifications/professional experience. item.title: Benefits Director Congressional And Legislative Affairs
item.description: Summary This position serves as a Director, Benefits Legislative Affairs Service in the Office of Congressional and Legislative Affairs. The assignment requires experience exercising a full range of managerial and supervisory responsibilities over a team of Congressional Relations Officers. Further, the position requires familiarity with the legislative and appropriations process, congressional activities, oversight, and concerns associated with the Department of Veterans Affairs. Duties ** *THIS IS NOT A VIRTUAL POSITION, YOU MUST LIVE WITHIN OR BE WILLING TO RELOCATE WITHIN A COMMUTABLE DISTANCE OF THE DUTY LOCATION*** Major Duties : Leads and manages the Benefits Legislative Affairs Service team within the Office of Congressional and Legislative Affairs. Acts as liaison between the senior officials in VA's Administrations, field facilities, and other staff offices and the Office of Congressional and Legislative Affairs in communicating information on VA programs, policies, and legislation affecting the Department and in developing and maintaining good relations with Congress. Establishes operational guidelines and manages day-to-day activities of the Benefits Legislative Affairs Service Staff. Monitors and analyzes inquiries and correspondence and requests related to congressional interest from Members of Congress for the Secretary and/or Deputy Secretary and other Veterans Affairs officials. Monitors and tracks congressional interests that could affect the Department of Veterans Affairs through personal contacts with members and key congressional staff; through congressional inquiries and correspondence; through daily review of legislative calendars, Congressional Record, and other documentary sources of information; through review of information provided by professional staff; and through personal contacts with high-level officials in other federal agencies and the White House. Represents OCLA and the Assistant Secretary at meetings with the Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries and other entities to review planned and pending legislation, and policy and program issues as they relate to upcoming hearings. Provides guidance to witnesses on testimony and protocol. Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8:00am - 4:30pm EST. Location: The selectee will be required to report on-site at 810 Vermont Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20420. Return to Office (RTO): RTO mandates are in affect and selectees will be required to report to in person work unless they have an approved exemption. Telework: Available - Ad Hoc telework (situational telework) as determined by the agency policy. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Position Description/PD#: PD702690 (Supervisory Management & Program Analyst) Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Financial Disclosure Report: Not required Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized Requirements Conditions of employment You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job To be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process. In addition to the application and questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job. Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959 You may be required to serve a probationary period Subject to background/security investigation Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements ( https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents ). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued identification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment. As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you may be required to serve a one year probationary period or two year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your one year probationary period or two year trial period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. Qualifications To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 10/29/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement : Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement. For a GS-15 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-14. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials. If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade. Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to some former Federal employees applying for reinstatement, as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment. See the Required Document section below for more information regarding the SF-50s needed to verify time-in-grade. You may qualify based on your experience and/as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-14 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization. Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Serving as the primary liaison to congressional offices and committee staff by maintaining effective working relationships that supported the advancement of legislative priorities. Managing all aspects of congressional hearings by drafting statements, coordinating pre and post hearing questions, and preparing witnesses on testimony and protocol. Exercising managerial authority their team's over workforce planning, operational execution, and strategic initiatives by evaluating staff performance, directing work assignments, and ensuring program objectives were met. Establishing operational goals and long range work plans to guide service wide execution and resolve issues involving overlapping responsibilities. Evidence of this specialized experience must be supported by detailed documentation of like duties performed in positions held on your resume. You will also need to provide work experience information such as hours per week, full-time/part-time status, and starting/ending dates of employment (month and year format) to establish you have one (1) full year of specialized experience at the required grade level. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religions; spiritual; community; student; social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Note : Resume must include job title and employer name, number of hours worked per week, start and end dates (including month and year), list of duties and responsibilities for each position held. In addition, if the experience was a federal position, you must list the grade for each position held. Failure to include this information may result in an ineligible rating. A full year of work is considered to be 40 hours of work per week. Part-time experience will be credited on the basis of time actually spent in appropriate activities. Applicants wishing to receive credit for such experience must indicate clearly the nature of their duties and responsibilities in each position and the number of hours a week spent in such employment. Physical Requirements: The work is primarily sedentary, although some slight physical effort may be required. For more information on these qualification standards, please visit the United States Office of Personnel Management's website at http://://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/ . The Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP) and Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provide eligible displaced Federal/VA competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. To be qualified you must submit appropriate documentation (a copy of the agency notice, your most recent performance rating, and your most recent SF-50 noting current position, grade level, and duty location) and be found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be found well qualified, applicants must meet the following qualifications: Led long-range operational and strategic planning for the Benefits Legislative Affairs Service by setting organizational objectives, aligning resources, and resolving cross-functional challenges that affected program execution. Directed program-level assessments of legislative initiatives by evaluating implementation effectiveness, measuring outcomes for targeted veteran populations, and recommending strategic improvements to ensure mission accomplishment.
