item.title: Public Policy Intern Summer 2027
item.description: Anticipated End Date: 2026-12-31 Position Title: Public Policy Intern - Summer 2027 Job Description: Public Policy Intern – Summer 2027 Location: District of Columbia (Washington, DC) This role requires associates to work from the posted locations full-time, enabling consistent face-to-face collaboration, teamwork, and direct engagement. This policy promotes an environment built on in-person interaction, communication, and immediate support. Please note that per our policy on hybrid/virtual work, candidates not within a reasonable commuting distance from the posting location(s) will not be considered for employment, unless accommodation is granted as required by law. The Public Policy Intern will support Elevance Health’s public policy team by analyzing federal and state policy developments affecting healthcare and preparing policy summaries and other written materials. Working with team members, the intern will contribute to the development of public policy positions and strategic initiatives. The Public Policy Internship program is a 12-week, full-time program running from May 17th, 2027 – August 6th, 2027. This internship is offered in partnership with Indiana University’s Capital Campus program, with recruitment focused on Indiana University students. How you will make an impact: Track federal and state legislation, regulations, and other developments affecting healthcare Review policy proposals to identify key provisions, proposed changes to existing policy, and potential implications for the organization and people it serves Draft issue briefs, policy summaries, and presentations to support internal discussions and policy development Attend policy briefings and create detailed summaries to document key insights Assist team members in developing and refining public policy positions, recommendations, and responses to policy proposals Minimum Qualifications : Currently enrolled in a BA/BS or an MA/MS degree program in public policy, health policy, public health, political science, health administration, business, or related major. Candidates pursuing other majors who have demonstrated interest in or experience with public policy will also be considered. Preferred Skills, Capabilities and Experiences : Interest in public policy and the healthcare industry Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an interest in developing presentation skills Strong problem-solving, strategic-thinking, analytical, and organizational skills. Familiarity with Microsoft Office products, including AI tools such as Copilot. Candidates graduating in Dec 2027 or May 2028 with a 3.2 GPA or higher are preferred. Other candidates who meet the minimum qualifications will also be considered. If this job is assigned to any Government Business Division entity, the applicant and incumbent fall under a 'sensitive position' work designation and may be subject to additional requirements beyond those associates outside Government Business Divisions. Requirements include but are not limited to more stringent and frequent background checks and/or government clearances, segregation of duties principles, role specific training, monitoring of daily job functions, and sensitive data handling instructions. Associates in these jobs must follow the specific policies, procedures, guidelines, etc. as stated by the Government Business Division in which they are employed. For candidates working in person or virtually in the below locations, the salary* range for this specific position is $19.78 to $28.26 Location(s): District of Columbia (Washington, DC) In addition to your salary, Elevance Health offers benefits such as a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). The salary offered for this specific position is based on a number of legitimate, non-discriminatory factors set by the Company. The Company is fully committed to ensuring equal pay opportunities for equal work regardless of gender, race, or any other category protected by federal, state, and local pay equity laws. * The salary range is the range Elevance Health in good faith believes is the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of this posting. This range may be modified in the future and actual compensation may vary from posting based on geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level. Even within the range, the actual compensation will vary depending on the above factors as well as market/business considerations. No amount is wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable under the terms and conditions of the applicable policies and plans. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole discretion, consistent with the law. Job Level: Non-Management Non-Exempt Workshift: Job Family: ADM > Intern Please be advised that Elevance Health only accepts resumes for compensation from agencies that have a signed agreement with Elevance Health. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Elevance Health. Who We Are Elevance Health is a health company dedicated to improving lives and communities – and making healthcare simpler. We are a Fortune 25 company with a longstanding history in the healthcare industry, looking for leaders at all levels of the organization who are passionate about making an impact on our members and the communities we serve. How We Work At Elevance Health, we are creating a culture that is designed to advance our strategy but will also lead to personal and professional growth for our associates. Our values and behaviors are the root of our culture. They are how we achieve our strategy, power our business outcomes and drive our shared success - for our consumers, our associates, our communities and our business. We offer a range of market-competitive total rewards that include merit increases, paid holidays, Paid Time Off, and incentive bonus programs (unless covered by a collective bargaining agreement), medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability benefits, 401(k) +match, stock purchase plan, life insurance, wellness programs and financial education resources, to name a few. Elevance Health operates in a Hybrid Workforce Strategy. Unless specified as primarily virtual by the hiring manager, associates are required to work at an Elevance Health location at least once per week, and potentially several times per week. Specific requirements and expectations for time onsite will be discussed as part of the hiring process. The health of our associates and communities is a top priority for Elevance Health. We require all new candidates in certain patient/member-facing roles to become vaccinated against COVID-19 and Influenza. If you are not vaccinated, your offer will be rescinded unless you provide an acceptable explanation. Elevance Health will also follow all relevant federal, state and local laws. Elevance Health is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, citizenship status, color, creed, disability, ethnicity, genetic information, gender (including gender identity and gender expression), marital status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status or any other status or condition protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. Applicants who require accommodation to participate in the job application process should submit the following form: Accessibility Accommodation Request Form and a member of the team will be in contact. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws, including, but not limited to, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act. Prospective employees required to be screened under Florida law should review the education and awareness resources at HB531 | Florida Agency for Health Care Administration . item.title: Federal Affairs Coordinator And Legislative Aide
item.description: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) is the premier grassroots organization focused on advocating solutions to the country’s greatest challenges. We recognize that tens of millions of Americans are frustrated with the extreme partisanship in government that keeps common-sense reforms from being passed, and instead seek to stand with policy leaders who are committed to finding a better way. Americans for Prosperity is part of the Stand Together philanthropic community. As the Federal Affairs Coordinator and Legislative Aide , you will keep our Federal Government Affairs team running at its best while supporting our federal lobbyists with legislative research and bill tracking. Reporting to the Director of Federal Government Affairs, you will manage the operations, budget, and communications that free our team to focus on winning public policy change that expands freedom and opportunity. This is a high-visibility, high-trust role for a skilled administrator with Capitol Hill or advocacy experience, sound judgment, and a bias for action. You will support three national brands (Americans for Prosperity, Concerned Veterans for America, and The LIBRE Initiative) and work regularly with congressional offices, coalition partners, and senior leadership. How You Will Contribute Team Operations and Knowledge Systems Manage daily operations for the federal government affairs team across AFP, CVA, and The LIBRE Initiative Maintain team calendars, internal trackers, shared tools, and legislative databases Budget and Finance Track the team budget in EPS with the Director of Federal Government Affairs, and compare actual spending against plan Process invoices and p-card expense reports in Concur, working with finance and accounting teams on time and with accuracy Prepare budget reports and support quarterly financial reviews for leadership Systems and Communications Send Quorum email blasts for the federal affairs team and train a backup to keep operations running Keep the team’s web content accurate and aligned with organizational messaging Run the legislative scorecard process, including vote tracking, coordination with policy staff, and timely publication Manage technology systems and software subscriptions, and work with IT on troubleshooting and purchases Legislative Support Research and analyze bills, amendments, and policy issues across all three brands Track bills through committee and floor votes, and keep the team informed of every move Attend committee hearings, floor sessions, events, and press conferences on behalf of the team What You Will Bring 3–5+ years of experience in operations, administration, or government affairs Proven ability to manage competing priorities with precision and composure in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment with limited supervision Exceptional attention to detail, organizational discipline, and written and verbal communication skills Proficiency with Microsoft Office, project management tools, and legislative platforms such as Quorum, Airtable, and IQ Stand Out Candidates Will Also Bring Experience on Capitol Hill or at a national advocacy organization Familiarity with Concur, EPS, and Quorum Genuine enthusiasm for the mission and values of Americans for Prosperity and free-market advocacy What We Offer Competitive benefits: Enjoy a 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting, flexible time off, comprehensive health and dental plans, plus wellness and mental health support through Peloton and Talkspace. A meaningful career: Join a passionate community of over 1,300 employees dedicated to improving lives and driving innovative solutions to complex social challenges. Commitment to growth: Thrive in a non-hierarchical environment that empowers employees to discover, develop and apply their unique talents. For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $70,000–$100,000 per year. This role may also be eligible for additional bonus compensation designed to align total compensation with an employee’s overall contribution to the organization. Our Principles-Based Management™ (PBM) compensation philosophy is grounded in an individualized approach that rewards the long-term value each person creates for the organization. Compensation decisions are informed by a variety of factors, including relevant experience, capabilities, demonstrated skills, role responsibilities, and expected contribution. Consistent with this approach, base salary may vary within or outside of the anticipated range based on these considerations. $70,000 - $100,000 a year Our Values: Working for an organization within the Stand Together philanthropic community is different from many other places. The culture is deeply rooted in Principle Based Management® (PBM®), a framework guided by the principles that drive human progress, such as dignity, openness, and bottom-up empowerment. PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. That is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, and respect. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: POSITION OBJECTIVE: Implement the public policy and regulatory programs in accordance with the policies established by the voting delegates and as interpreted by the Board of Directors of the American Farm Bureau Federation. Advocate on behalf of Farm Bureau policies related to food, nutritional, and other agriculture related topics. REPORTS TO: Managing Director, Government Affairs LOCATION: Washington, DC; eligible for hybrid telework under AFBF Policy PAY RANGE: $135,000 - $150,000 annually; commensurate with experience DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES: Represent Farm Bureau and advocate the organization’s policy positions to Congress, the Executive branch, the media and other private sector organizations. Present Farm Bureau views in speeches before appropriate groups, public forums, and Farm Bureau meetings. Develop and implement long- and short-term action plans that lead to the accomplishment of Farm Bureau’s policies on food, nutrition, and other issues as assigned. In collaboration with members of the Public Policy Department, develop and implement long- and short-term action plans that lead to the accomplishment of Farm Bureau’s policies and other issues as assigned. Prepare and deliver remarks to public audiences, regulators and regulatory agencies, as well as draft congressional testimony, letters to Capitol Hill, memoranda for internal distribution within Farm Bureau, public-facing Policy Intel reports and detailed regulatory comments on Federal rulemakings. Leverage support for Farm Bureau policy by establishing and maintaining positive working relationships with: Appropriate personnel in assigned Congressional and federal administrative and regulatory agencies State Farm Bureau leadership and staff Industry trade associations and private sector coalitions Industry partners in food and agribusiness sectors Keep abreast of legislative developments, rulings and rulemaking proceedings and prepare analyses and/or statements on these matters. Organize and participate in meetings and conferences in appropriate subject areas as needed and serve on special committees and coalitions. Work with state Farm Bureaus in visits to Washington, D.C. and make presentations at meetings called by the states. Serve as a resource person for AFBF Communications team in the development and dissemination of advocacy materials. Serve as the primary on-the-record spokesperson and media resource on issues within the assigned portfolio. RELATIONSHIPS: Proactively research and communicate policy developments to Farm Bureau leadership, staff and state staff. Develop and maintain a collaborative information-sharing strategy that ensures relevant insights are disseminated to appropriate AFBF team members and organization leadership. EDUCATION OR TRAINING REQUIRED: Bachelor’s degree or higher EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED: Minimum five (5) years public policy experience Strong operational understanding of executive and legislative branches of federal government Knowledge or background in production agriculture PREFERRED EXPERIENCE/TRAINING/SKILLS: Strong understanding of food and nutritional issues Legislative and/or Executive Branch experience Trade association experience desired Understanding of the Farm Bureau organization, including its purpose, structure, and operation OTHER REQUIREMENTS: Travel (approximately 20%) and willingness to work weekends as needed Public Speaking Registration as a federal lobbyist. Candidates with additional experience are encouraged to apply. Compensation will be commensurate with qualifications. TO APPLY: Submit a cover letter and resume.

item.title: Public Policy Advocacy Internship Spring 2027
item.description: We are pleased to offer an outstanding and substantive internship program for the nation's best and brightest young leaders. At the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, you will obtain a hands-on, meaningful work experience designed to meet your academic and career goals. Our internships offer opportunities in research, writing, database management, policy, communications, and event preparation. During the internship, you will network with colleagues and senior executives while participating in educational and professional activities designed to enhance your experience. PROGRAM OVERVIEW: The Chamber Internship Program is a one-of-a-kind opportunity to learn at the world's largest business organization. In addition to directly supporting a team in the organization, interns have an opportunity to participate in a variety of programming that will help build professional skills and networks. Responsibilities for interns typically include research, drafting memos, content creation, and event planning and coordination. Specific responsibilities vary by department and semester. The Chamber also offers robust programming each semester to support professional development and networking for interns. These opportunities include company-wide meetings and social events, intern-exclusive discussions with senior executives such as the CEO, the Chief Policy Officer, and the President of the Foundation, as well as a resume review and interview preparation workshop. The internship is expected to run from February 1 through April 9. Interns work a part-time hybrid schedule and are expected to be in the office at least three days a week at our U.S. Chamber of Commerce headquarters in downtown Washington, D.C. Fully remote applicants will not be considered. Interns will be responsible for making their own housing accommodations if needed. This is a paid internship, and students may also receive academic credit if they meet the criteria set by their school. The hourly rate for this position is between $18.00 and $20.00 per hour. This internship is open to current college or graduate students, as well as individuals who have graduated within the past six months. DEPARTMENT MATCHING The Public Policy & Advocacy teams shape U.S. and global policy on critical issues including economic growth, energy, cybersecurity, employment, healthcare, and strategic advocacy. Interns will support policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications efforts that advance the Chamber’s pro-business priorities across public and private sectors. After you submit your resume, our Talent Acquisition team will review it. If your skills match what we are looking for, the relevant department will reach out for an interview. Please review the departments below closely. In the application, please indicate your top two department preferences. Cyber, Space, & National Security PolicyThe National Security Policy division advocates on behalf of the Chamber's members who have a direct stake in cybersecurity, defense, space, and supply chain security policy. Interns support the team with preparation, research, and materials for major events including the March Aerospace event and roundtables across cyber, space, and defense, as well as international trip preparation. This role is ideal for candidates with an interest in national security, technology policy, and Capitol Hill engagement. Economic PolicyThe U.S. Chamber's Economic Policy team serves as an in-house quantitative resource for member companies, state and local chambers, and policy teams across the building. Interns play a hands-on role tracking economic data releases and trends to support outlook briefings, assisting as quantitative consultants on domestic and international policy work, and exploring new applications of AI in the team's day-to-day operations. This is a great fit for candidates with a strong interest in economics, data analysis, and applied policy research. Employment PolicyThe Employment Policy team advances the Chamber's workforce, education, and labor policy priorities on behalf of American businesses. Interns take on substantive ownership across three core areas: supporting planning and execution of the Child Care Fly-In (a key grant deliverable), revamping the America Works homepage to strengthen external communications on education and workforce issues, and helping prepare members for ILO negotiations on chemical hazards and AI in the workplace. This role is ideal for candidates interested in labor policy, workforce development, and international employer advocacy. Global Energy InstituteThe U.S. Chamber's Global Energy Institute unifies energy stakeholders and policymakers behind a common strategy to ensure America's supply of fuel and power is adequate, stable, and affordable, while protecting national security and improving the environment. Interns support the team across three core areas: event logistics and stakeholder engagement for high-profile convenings, policy research across the electric generation, permitting, and international energy portfolios, and strategic communications including one-pagers, blog posts, newsletters, and briefing materials. A great fit for candidates interested in energy policy, advocacy, and the intersection of policy and communications. Government AffairsThe Government Affairs division is the Chamber's lobbying team, headquartered in Washington with regional offices across the country, championing pro-business priorities and advocating for America's free enterprise system on Capitol Hill. Interns support the team with congressional hearing preparation, drafting member briefing profiles, organizing testimony materials, tracking legislation, and supporting policy forums and Hill activities. Interns are also encouraged to attend Hill meetings and events, gaining firsthand exposure to the legislative process and the Chamber's advocacy work. Housing Policy The Housing Policy team leads the Chamber’s national initiative to address America’s housing shortage by advancing pro-growth policies that increase housing supply and affordability. Interns support the team across three core areas: land use and permitting reform, housing finance and capital access, and workforce and immigration policy. Responsibilities include policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications support to advance the Chamber’s housing advocacy efforts. This role is ideal for candidates interested in housing policy, economic growth, and public policy development. Chamber Technology Engagement CenterThe Chamber Technology Engagement Center (C_TEC) is at the forefront of the Chamber's work on emerging technology policy, including artificial intelligence, robotics, and quantum computing. Interns play a direct role in drafting white papers on these cutting-edge topics and tracking technology legislation across states — work that directly shapes the Chamber's policy positions and thought leadership. This is an ideal opportunity for candidates passionate about technology policy, innovation, and the future of the digital economy. Applications are accepted until Thursday, October 12. Interviews will be conducted in November & December. This internship requires U.S. work authorization and is open to candidates with Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and/or Optional Practical Training (OPT). We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

item.title: Assistant Associate Director Of Government Affairs
item.description: Position: Assistant/Associate Director of Government Affairs Reports to: Director of Government Affairs Start Date: As soon as possible Status: Full Time, Exempt Location: Washington, DC Application Deadline: November 30, 2026 Position Are you interested in joining an influential organization that is changing the way Washington thinks and talks about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and U.S. Middle East policy at a turning point in US politics? J Street’s Government Affairs team is seeking a legislative professional to help advance its advocacy strategy. This individual will lobby a portfolio of Congressional offices, help draft and shape legislation, and collaborate with staff, policy experts, and J Street leaders to redefine the US-Israel relationship, pursue legislative opportunities to rebuild the US-Palestinian relationship, and create the conditions to facilitate regional peace. The ideal candidate will be aligned with J Street’s mission and principles , as well as a self-starting, entrepreneurial thinker with keen political instincts and strong attention to detail. They thrive on hitting ambitious goals and are excited by the challenge of changing the dynamics that shape the discussion of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in Congress. Our Core Values At J Street, everything we do is grounded in three core values that guide how we work, collaborate, and show up for our mission. Impactful — We act with intention. We measure success not just by what we do, but by the progress we make and the change we help bring about. Adaptable — We treat every challenge as an invitation to think creatively, reframe the problem, and find a better path forward. Aligned — We are united by shared principles and an unwavering commitment to our mission. Our strength comes from believing in what we're building together Specific Responsibilities This is an in-person job, with the expectation that four days are in the office or on Capitol Hill (approximately 20% a week). Work from home option is available for Fridays and other days as needed. Managing and directly lobbying a portfolio of Congressional offices by deepening existing relationships and growing new ones between Members of Congress and J Street; Formulating and guiding the execution of tactics and strategies to move Members of Congress and advance legislative and policy priorities; Draft talking points, legislative vehicles, communication to Hill offices, as well as assist in maintaining the operations of the Government Affairs team; Maintaining up-to-date awareness and deep knowledge of relevant legislative initiatives and policy developments on our issue; and Contributing to the organization’s strategic advocacy planning as a core member of the Government Affairs Team. Ideal Qualifications and Skills Alignment with the organization’s mission: Familiarity with issues related to the US-Israel relationship and the American Jewish community, and alignment with J Street’s mission and goals. Legislative Experience: The ideal candidate will have a minimum of four years of legislative/lobbying experience with a preference toward experience working in a Hill office. Writing Skills: This position requires the ability to quickly draft and edit legislative analysis, talking points, and other materials. Strong Relationship-building and interpersonal Skills: Intentional about building and maintaining relationships, including maintaining trust. High EQ, as well as strong presentation skills. Collaborative and constructive attitude: The candidate must be able to collaborate effectively, and work closely across departments within the organization. This is not a siloed job. Issue fluency: Middle East/US foreign policy expertise, with a solid understanding of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and how it plays out in American politics. Attention to detail: You can manage many projects at once while maintaining a commitment to a detail-oriented approach. Adherence to deadlines: Competence in working well and quickly under tight deadlines, utilizing current business technology and data management. Nice to Haves: Experience in drafting, tracking or lobbying must-pass legislation including appropriations bills and the National Defense Authorization Act; Proficient in using AI as a means of completing repetitive tasks, conducting research, or analyzing large datasets and; Experience working with relevant committees of jurisdiction, including SFRC/HFAC, as well HASC/SASC. Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this full-time exempt position is $72,000-$87,000 The final salary offer will be determined after reviewing relevant factors, including but not limited to skill sets; relevant experience; internal equity; and other business and organizational needs. Our comprehensive benefits package includes: Unlimited personal time off Sick leave Generous parental and family paid leave (up to 12 weeks) Paid time off on many federal and Jewish holidays Health and dental and vision insurance Company-paid life insurance A 401k program with a competitive employer match and unmatched contributions Commuter benefits A Flexible Spending Account Health Savings Account with an employer contribution Professional Development Funding Six Week Paid Sabbatical J Street recognizes a staff bargaining unit affiliated with IFPTE Local 70, a union for non-profit workers. This position is included in J Street’s bargaining unit and is covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. Physical Requirements There are no extraordinary physical requirements for the performance of the essential functions of this position. J Street will make reasonable accommodation to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. To Apply We are excited to receive applications from a broad range of applicants as we grow our organization to better reflect the diversity of the communities who care about our mission. Please submit the items listed below: Resume Cover Letter that explains why you are interested and qualified (optional) Answer three position application questions that help us get to know you List of Three References Please apply by November 30, 2026. At J Street we value an inclusive, welcoming, and diverse workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to understanding and valuing each other’s perspectives at all levels of the organization thereby creating a culture that allows us to better serve our employees, and the communities we work with. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law. This policy applies with regard to all aspects of one’s employment and fellowship, including hiring, transfer, promotion, compensation, eligibility for benefits, and termination. J Street is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Icba Government Relations Vice President Congressional Relations
item.description: The Vice President, Congressional Relations is responsible for advocating ICBA’s legislative policy positions before the Congress (both House and Senate), financial regulatory agencies, and the Executive Branch. This role also assists and informs ICBA members on congressional activities and with policymaker interaction. Additional responsibilities include communicating association policies to members, other financial groups, and the media. This position is open to applicants in the Washington, DC area. What You’ll Do Maintain continuous contact with members of Congress, their personal office staff and key committee staff. Orchestrate grassroots/grass tops lobbying efforts to motivate members and influence Congress. Attend PAC events, both in-town and out-of-town. Assist association members visiting Congressional offices and agencies. Develop, draft and negotiate bill language and/or amendments. Cover and report on Congressional hearings and legislative markups. Work with association members to formulate association positions. Assist in developing strategies for lobbying Congress in coordination with legislative and regulatory teams. Assist with drafting congressional testimony, letters, position papers, regulatory comments, and articles. Help thoroughly prepare association members testifying before Congress and regulatory agencies. Prepare for, attend and report on association committee meetings and other events. Respond in a timely manner to banker and press inquiries. Establish and maintain relationship with other lobbyists, trade associations and coalitions. Work with state banking associations on Federal legislation Represent association at industry conferences, coalition meetings and other gatherings Areas of legislative responsibility: Monitor and influence legislative and regulatory developments in assigned areas. Analyze legislation in assigned areas for impact upon community banks and their customers. Assist other members of the congressional and regulatory teams on priority lobbying issues. What You Bring Minimum BA degree: law or public policy degree preferred Minimum seven (7) years of related government relations or trade association experience, including working knowledge of banking and financial services issues; Congressional experience preferred Strong written, analytical and oral communication skills Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to interface well with members of Congress, Hill staff, member bankers and ICBA staff colleagues Able to work well both independently and as a member of a team Ability for travel 10% We recognize that candidates may not meet every qualification listed. If your background and experience are close to what we’re seeking, we encourage you to apply. Benefits of Working at ICBA Generous and competitive benefits package 401(k) savings plan offering 100% employer match of up to 6% of annual earnings. Hybrid work environment, monthly work from home stipends, and flexible work hours Fitness discounts, telemedicine, on-demand therapy, and work-life balance tools Tuition reimbursement and allowances for professional development Frequent company social events Friendly and inclusive workplace culture The target annual salary range for this role is currently $125,000 – 175,000 based on a regular, full-time schedule. The amount of compensation offered will be determined by several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications, location, market data and internal equity. ICBA is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. ICBA does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA)’s guiding mission is to create and promote environments where community banks flourish. We are: • Dedicated advocates providing community bankers, policymakers and the public with authoritative insights and resources to support and strengthen community banking. • Knowledgeable, applying their expertise to offer personalized service that addresses the distinct challenges and opportunities facing community banks. • Community-centered, driving meaningful change that strengthens community banks and the communities they serve. We turn commitment into action and deliver real results. ICBA’s workplace culture is built on our core values: • Caring -We support and prioritize your well-being and professional growth. • Connected - We foster strong relationships that create meaningful impact. • Collaboration – We are team-oriented and results driven where diverse perspectives are valued, and innovative ideas are encouraged to achieve our common goals. Join ICBA and further your career while making a lasting impact

item.title: Government Affairs Intern
item.description: A bout the Position: The National Association of Counties (NACo) is offering a paid internship within the Government Affairs department. This internship provides a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in federal advocacy, policy analysis and county government practices. This internship will run from mid-January 2027 to mid-May 2027 , with start and end dates subject to the availability of the candidate. Candidates must be available to provide on-site assistance to the Government Affairs team at NACo’s 2027 Legislative Conference from February 19 – 23 in Washington, D.C. As part of NACo’s Government Affairs team, you will gain significant exposure to the federal legislative process, explore advocacy strategies and make valuable connections with government officials, Congressional staff and other legislative professionals. NACo is a friendly, fast-paced work environment with a bipartisan, mission-driven team. An ideal candidate will thrive in a strategic, nonpartisan political environment designed to advance the policies and priorities of our members. Candidates should have a strong understanding of and interest in the U.S. political system, including local and regional government and its nexus with federal programs and regulations. Key Responsibilities: Researching and analyzing impacts of legislation and regulations Authoring advocacy updates on regulatory and legislative actions Learning and utilizing software and computer systems utilized by the Government Affairs department Organizing materials, such as agendas, briefing documents and attendee packets, for conference sessions and meetings Supporting NACo Government Affairs team at in-person meetings and conferences Other duties as assigned Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree and are at least a sophomore in good standing, or have earned a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university Excellent oral and written communications skills Ability to meet deadlines and work well under pressure Knowledge of and interest in local government policies and practices Prior internship experience a plus, particularly in government affairs, on Capitol Hill or for a state or local government Hours/Salary: Expected to work 10-15 hours per week. This internship pays $18.40 per hour. Application Procedures: Please send a cover letter and indicate your availability (approximate number of hours per week available to work and approximate start and end dates). Applications are processed on a rolling basis until all available positions are filled, so applying early is encouraged. Location and Travel: The internship is based in our NACo’s Washington, D.C. office and will be primarily in person.

item.title: Associate Government Affairs
item.description: Who We Are: Raben is a public policy, strategic communications and organizational consulting firm. Our talented and passionate team champions diversity, equity, and justice as core values that ignite our mission for impactful change in corporate, nonprofit, government, and foundation work. Our changemakers work to solve real-world problems and inspire lasting changes through our four service offerings: strategic communications, government affairs, issue campaigns, and culture, strategy, & organizational design. We have been fueled by insightful strategy, creative tactics, and plain old hustle for over 20 years. We are people of color, women, immigrants, disabled, and LGBTQ. Spend time with us and you will quickly learn we value smarts, creativity, and audaciousness in just about all we do… and a sense of humor is a contractual must. Learn more at raben.co. What We Seek: We seek an AssociateAssociate to join our Government Affairs practice in our Washington, DC office to support Raben client teams and engagements. Associates have hands-on expertise, contextual knowledge, strong critical thinking abilities, the desire to develop and the tactical skills to advance the strategic mission and vision of Raben and further the development and success of our Government Affairs practice in providing excellent client services and engaging prospective clients. Our successful candidate will have a high degree of initiative, personal resilience, attention to detail, intellectual engagement in the subject-matter at hand, and a concierge-like approach to client services. This position is located in our DC office and follows a hybrid schedule with at least two days per week in office. We offer schedule flexibility, while prioritizing a consistent and meaningful in-office presence to support collaboration and team engagement. Responsibilities: Serve as a tactician on designated teams, conducting legislative and policy research, drafting memos and reports, monitoring legislation, monitoring and summarizing legislative hearings, and conducting outreach to Hill offices for scheduling, information gathering and coordination. Ensure timely, responsive client service delivery, including tracking internal deliverables, responding to client requests, capturing notes and action items in team meetings, and proactive troubleshooting. Assist in the planning, coordination, and staffing of meetings, convenings, conference calls, panels, Lobby Days, etc., including – venue logistics, registrations, marketing and outreach, attendee and speaker communications, on-site support, vendor management, etc. Contribute to the organizational goals of the firm’s Government Affairs and Policy Counsel practice group. Other duties as assigned. Requirements Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required; work, internship, or volunteer experience on the Hill is a plus. Strong proficiency with internet research, Microsoft Word, Sharepoint, Excel and PowerPoint required; professional experience with social media applications and web content management systems a plus. A collaborative and relationship-building mindset. Must be able to proactively identify potential challenges/conflicts and communicate with team members with a problem-solving approach. Strong writing, layout and editing skills; experience with desktop publishing tools. Strong oral and written communication skills are a non-negotiable requirement. Candidates must have the demonstrable ability to quickly produce clear, compelling written collateral and communicate professionally and diplomatically with a wide range of staff, clients, partners and stakeholders. Ability to thrive and manage shifting priorities under tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Demonstrable project and time management skills across multiple assignments with many moving parts. Prior event coordination experience preferred. Application Instructions: To apply, please submit an application and resume via our online job portal. At this time, we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship. If you need accommodation during the recruitment process, please email your needs to careers@raben.co . Salary Range and Benefits: Our salary for this role is $55,000 per year. In addition to a great degree of autonomy in work and projects, our colleagues enjoy a suite of benefits such as health, dental, and vision insurance, unlimited PTO, flexibility in schedule, a rich professional development curriculum, a 3% 401K match, yearly employer FSA contribution, work from home flexibility, and many more. Raben finds it quite natural to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, aspiring to live the values of equity in everything we do. Salary Description $55,000 annually

item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Apply here - https://secure.builtapp.com/rila/jobs/fd89422c RILA is growing! At the Retail Industry Leaders Association (RILA) , we convene decision-makers, advocate for the retail industry, and promote operational excellence and innovation. Our aim is bold but simple: to elevate a dynamic industry by transforming the environment in which retailers operate. We are a dynamic, collaborative, team-oriented trade association in Washington, DC. Our employees are passionate about customer service and supporting our members and each other, and we are adding to the team! What we are looking for: Position Summary: The Coordinator, Government Affairs is an entry‑level position supporting the work of RILA’s Public Affairs department. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Government Affairs, this role assists with the day‑to‑day execution of member‑facing activities, policy tracking and research, and communications that advance RILA's broader public policy priorities. This position plays a key role in logistics, content development, member engagement, and internal coordination to support the department’s initiatives. It is well suited for a motivated early‑career government affairs professional with strong communication, organizational, and analytical skills. Position Responsibilities: Project Coordination & Administration: Serve as an internal project coordinator by tracking timelines, documenting progress, and aligning deliverables with relevant team members. Provide administrative and coordination support to the SVP, GA and the broader Public Affairs team as needed. Identify opportunities to improve internal processes, tools, and resource delivery. Policy Research & Content Development: Conduct policy research and prepare briefing materials, reports, talking points, and background documents. Draft and support delivery of written member communications, including newsletters, issue briefs, research summaries, meeting notes, and internal memos. Member Engagement & Meeting Support: Assist with coordination of virtual and in‑person member committee meetings, legislative fly‑ins, and conference calls. Schedule meetings with policymakers and assist with outreach to coalition partners. Systems & Information Management: Maintain and update databases and digital assets (e.g., Salesforce), including committee rosters, registration links, and public‑facing and member web content. Success Metrics & Performance Indicators: Timely and accurate coordination of meetings, communications, and deliverables. Member satisfaction with responsiveness and support. Quality, clarity, and accuracy of written materials and research outputs. Consistent and accurate maintenance of internal databases and public‑facing content. Ability to manage multiple responsibilities with attention to detail and follow‑through. Core Competencies: Project and Task Coordination. Written Communication and Editing. Stakeholder Service Orientation. Research and Information Synthesis. Database and Digital Content Management. Professional Growth Opportunities: This role provides opportunities for growth through increased responsibility in program coordination, public policy engagement, issue‑area expertise, and member communications. The Coordinator will gain exposure to national issues impacting the retail industry and build foundational experience working with corporate executives, government affairs professionals, policymakers, and external partners. What you will get from us: At RILA, you will find solid people. We do our best to learn and grow each day, driven by a passion for building leaders and cultivating an inclusive and collaborative culture. We promise that the work you do will matter and will have an impact on the vast retail industry and the communities our retailers serve. You will have an opportunity to grow professionally and develop new skills and we will challenge and support you in your professional journey. Consider becoming part of the RILA team - check out our RILA Careers page here and some RILA reviews here. Compensation & Benefits: $53,000 starting annual salary with overtime and bonus opportunities. Flexible and hybrid office environment (3 days in office). Affordable Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage (FSA/HSA options available). Employer-sponsored Life Insurance, STD, and LTD Coverage. 401(K)/Roth 401(K) Retirement Plan with employer match. Unlimited Paid Time Off + 12 Federal holiday closures. Professional development opportunities. Team outings/gatherings. *** RILA is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Application Instructions: Please submit a resume and statement of interest to https://secure.builtapp.com/rila/jobs/fd89422c explaining your interest in the role and how your experience aligns. Thanks!

item.title: Legislative Representative
item.description: Job Description The Agency You’ll Join: The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. We value leadership, transparency, fairness, and efficiency as we actively seek diverse talents from various sectors to join our team. For current job opportunities, visit our careers page. The Team You’ll Work With: **NOTE: THIS ROLE IS LOCATED IN WASHINGTON, DC.** The Office of Federal Affairs coordinates the City's interaction with the Federal administration and Congress. The office keeps the Mayor and City agencies informed about pending or important issues affecting the City. The office also advocates on behalf of the city and is the DC liaison between the City and other cities seeking to work together on federal issues. The Problems You’ll Solve: The Legislative Representative will keep the Mayor and City agencies informed about pending or important issues affecting the City. About You: - You must have detailed knowledge of the Federal legislative process and elected officials. - You can demonstrate the understanding of and experience with any combination of the following: the City legislative process, public policy analysis, New York City and State agency operations, and lobbying. Minimum Required Qualifications: - Bachelor’s Degree. - 2+ years of relevant experience in New York City and State agency ecosystem, legislative, and operations processes. RESEARCH PROJECTS COOR(MA)-MGR - 0527A Qualifications 1. Do you have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university? 2. Do you have an associate degree from an accredited college or university along with two (2) years of experience with administrative, analytic, coordinative, supervisory or liaison responsibilities? 3. Do you have a four-year high school diploma, or its educational equivalent approved by a state's Department of Education or a recognized accrediting organization along with four (4) years of experience as described in question "2" above? 4. Do you have a satisfactory combination of education and/or experience equivalent to that described in questions "1," "2," and/or "3" above? Additional Information The City of New York is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce and providing a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment based upon any legally protected status or protected characteristic, including but not limited to an individual's sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity, or pregnancy.

item.title: Supervisory Program Analyst Legislative
item.description: Summary This position is located in the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation's (PBGC), Communications Outreach and Legislative Affairs Department, Legislative Affairs Division. CONCURRENT ANNOUNCEMENT: THIS POSITION IS ALSO BEING ADVERTISED UNDER DELEGATED EXAMINING PROCEDURES UNDER ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER OPEA-COLAD-LAD-2713103835. IF YOU WISH TO BE CONSIDERED UNDER THAT ANNOUNCEMENT, PLEASE REVIEW TO DETERMINE IF YOU QUALIFY. Duties This position serves as an Understudy to the current Supervisory Management Analyst (Legislative), GS-0343-15 division manager. To ensure a successful transition, if selected, you will shadow the current incumbent. Once the incumbent vacates the position, you will transition into the position at the GS-15 grade level without further competition. The candidate selected for this position will: Work in coordination with the Chief Policy Officer and Policy, Research, and Analysis Department Director to coordinate and oversee review and analysis of legislative proposals and incorporate appropriate PBGC and Executive Branch views. Support development of policy options, communications products that implement legislation, and PBGC content in the President's Budget and reports to Congress. Coordinate PBGC responses to requests for technical assistance from congressional committees, congressional member offices, and other federal agencies concerning legislative items and the operation of PBGC programs. Develop outreach plans and conduct outreach to congressional staff, including notifications of agency actions and developments. Coordinate responses to questions and requests for further information, manage delivery of reports to Congress, and arrange briefings on PBGC developments. Monitor and review congressional hearings, retirement-related legislation, and PBGC-related policy proposals from other Executive Branch agencies and outside parties. Plan, direct, coordinate, and evaluate the work of subordinate staff to ensure the effective and efficient accomplishment of organizational goals and objectives. Requirements Conditions of employment You must be a U.S citizen. You may undergo a personnel security background investigation. Selective Service registration required for male applicants, unless exempt. 1-year probationary period required unless met during prior Federal service. Go through a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) process that requires two forms of identification from the Form I-9. Federal law requires verification of the identity and employment eligibility of all new hires in the U.S. Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment to determine your suitability for Federal employment, at the time requested by the agency. Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. 1-year supervisory probationary period required unless met during prior Federal service. Qualifications All qualification requirements must be met within 30 days of the announcement closing date. To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience qualifications and/or education for the grade at which you are requesting consideration. Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one year of specialized experience at the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service or equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the private sector reviewing complex pension or retirement related legislative and policy proposals; coordinating technical assistance or responses to congressional offices or federal agencies; developing congressional outreach or briefing materials to support agency programs and policy recommendations; and conducting analysis related to, or experience with private sector pension plan operations and regulation. Experience working for or with a Congressional committee or a member's staff is preferred. Examples include: leading multidisciplinary review of legislative proposals affecting pension insurance programs; coordinating technical analysis and clearance of communications to Congress; planning congressional outreach and briefings; and monitoring hearings, legislation, and external policy proposals for agency leadership. Time-In-Grade Requirement: In order to be eligible for this position, all current Federal employees must provide proof of meeting the time-in-grade requirement (i.e., at least 52 weeks of experience at the next lower grade level in the Federal service). This information must be in both your resume and on an SF-50. Those who do not provide proof of having met the time-in-grade requirement will be deemed ineligible for this position. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Education NO EDUCATION IS REQUIRED. Additional information To be considered under a special hiring authority such as the Schedule A appointing authority for persons with disabilities ; the direct-hire authority to appoint veterans with service-connected disabilities of 30 percent or more ; Peace Corps or VISTA service; or another excepted service/special hire authority, you must submit documentation to support your claim for eligibility with your application package. PBGC encourages qualified applicants with disabilities to apply. If you are requiring reasonable accommodations, please contact PBGC's Reasonable Accommodation Coordinator, Denorse Prince, at (202) 286-4026 or prince.denorse@pbgc.gov If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services. All Veterans are encouraged to visit CareerOne for resume writing tips and skill conversion terms. If you believe that you have been subjected to discrimination, you may contact the PBGC Office of Equal Employment Opportunity (OEEO): OEEO Main Office Phone: 202-229-4363 Email: EEO@PBGC.gov Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new window Learn more about federal benefits . Visit PBGC Benefits for information on our Agency Benefits offered. Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: Everytown for Gun Safety is seeking an experienced Director of Government Affairs to lead federal lobbying and advocacy efforts on Capitol Hill and with the Administration. We're looking for someone who knows how Washington works, has strong relationships with policymakers and congressional staff, and can turn legislative strategy into action. This is an opportunity for an experienced Hill staffer or federal lobbyist to put their relationships, political instincts, and expertise to work advancing gun violence prevention policies. As a senior member of the Government Affairs team, the Director will help shape and execute federal legislative strategy, engage key decision-makers, and advance the organization's priorities in Congress and across the Administration. This position will be based at our Washington, DC office, and will adhere to a hybrid work schedule. WE TRUST YOU TO: Federal Lobbying & Legislative Strategy • Lead federal lobbying and advocacy efforts before Congress and the Administration. • Develop and execute legislative strategies to advance the organization's federal gun violence prevention priorities. • Build and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, Administration officials, and key stakeholders. • Monitor legislative and political developments, identify opportunities, and advise leadership on strategy and engagement. • Represent Everytown in congressional meetings, legislative briefings, coalition meetings, and other external engagements. • Lead advocacy efforts during key legislative moments, including hearings, markups, floor votes, and other congressional activity. Advocacy & Coordination • Work with policy, political, communications, and research teams to align federal advocacy strategy and messaging. • Collaborate with national coalitions and advocacy partners to advance shared legislative priorities. • Develop briefing materials, talking points, and strategic recommendations to support federal lobbying efforts. QUALIFICATIONS: We're looking for someone with strong political instincts, an established network, and a commitment to preventing gun violence. The ideal candidate knows how to navigate Capitol Hill, build effective relationships, and move legislative priorities forward from day one. • Significant experience working on Capitol Hill, in federal lobbying, government affairs, or political advocacy. • Established relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and key federal stakeholders. • Deep understanding of Congress, the legislative process, and the federal political landscape. • Proven ability to develop and execute legislative strategies, navigate political challenges, and deliver results. • Strong communication skills, political judgment, and the ability to work effectively with policymakers and coalition partners. • A genuine commitment to gun violence prevention and Everytown's mission. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS The salary range for this position is $135,000 to $145,000 per year, depending on experience. Everytown offers a generous benefits package, including medical, vision, and dental insurance, paid time off, 401(k) matching, education assistance, and more. ABOUT THE HIRING PROCESS We are accepting applications on a rolling basis and will review applications as they are received. To be considered, applicants must submit both a cover letter and an updated resume. ** Applications missing either document will not be reviewed. DIVERSE WORKFORCE AND OPEN CULTURE Candidates who identify as members of historically underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply to Everytown. A diverse workforce and open culture are at the heart of our organization and vital to our success. Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. You can learn about the framework that guides our work by viewing Everytown's Organizations Values ABOUT EVERYTOWN FOR GUN SAFETY Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund (“Everytown for Gun Safety”) is the largest gun violence prevention organization in the country, with nearly 11 million supporters and more than 700,000 donors, including moms, mayors, survivors, students, and everyday Americans fighting for common-sense gun safety measures that can help save lives. Learn more at www.everytown.org and follow us @Everytown.

item.title: Senior Federal Lobbyist
item.description: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) is the premier grassroots organization focused on advocating solutions to the country’s greatest challenges. We recognize that tens of millions of Americans are frustrated with the extreme partisanship in government that keeps common-sense reforms from being passed, and instead seek to stand with policy leaders who are committed to finding a better way. Americans for Prosperity is part of the Stand Together philanthropic community. As a Senior Federal Lobbyist (internal title: Senior Federal Legislative Liaison) , you will serve as a principal advocate for AFP’s positions in Washington, D.C., working with the Director of Federal Affairs to shape and execute our federal legislative strategy. Your goal: break down the barriers that stand in the way of people realizing their full potential. You will focus on federal legislative advocacy in several policy areas but economics, energy, and AI and emerging technology or donor disclosure laws are particularly valuable areas of expertise. This role is ideal for an accomplished federal lobbyist with a deep Capitol Hill network and a record of moving policy. You will lead advocacy on AFP’s priority issues, represent the organization before Congress, federal agencies, and the executive branch, and guide coalitions and junior team members. You should share our commitment to advancing every individual’s right to economic opportunity through free markets. How You Will Contribute Lead AFP’s federal legislative advocacy on economics, energy, and AI and emerging technology , setting strategy and priorities with the Director of Federal Affairs Cultivate and leverage senior-level relationships with members of Congress, chiefs of staff, committee leadership, and federal agency and executive branch officials Represent AFP before Congress, federal agencies, and external audiences, including through testimony and formal comments Develop and execute multi-front legislative and regulatory campaigns, from bill introduction through enactment Anticipate legislative and regulatory trends, and advise leadership on risks, opportunities, and strategic responses Build and lead coalitions with trade associations, think tanks, and allied organizations to advance shared policy objectives Oversee the development of position papers, testimony, fact sheets, and other advocacy materials Partner with the policy, legal, communications, and research teams to align advocacy with organizational priorities Mentor and guide federal legislative liaisons and other government affairs team members What You Will Bring 8+ years of legislative or government affairs experience, including significant federal lobbying or Capitol Hill experience Proven track record of developing and executing government affairs strategies that produced legislative or regulatory results Established relationships and credibility with members of Congress, senior congressional staff, and federal agency officials Demonstrated experience representing an organization before Congress, federal agencies, and executive branch officials Deep knowledge of the federal legislative and regulatory process, with substantive expertise in economic, energy, or technology policy Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including testifying and presenting to senior policymakers Sound strategic judgment and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment Stand Out Candidates Will Also Bring Expertise in donor disclosure and donor privacy policy , including legislative and regulatory issues affecting nonprofit organizations Experience leading coalitions or managing outside lobbying partners Experience mentoring or managing government affairs professionals Deep knowledge of energy policy, AI policy, or emerging technology regulation Experience with lobbying disclosure compliance and registration requirements Enthusiasm for Stand Together’s vision and principled approach to solving problems, and a commitment to stewarding our culture , which champions values including transformation and innovation, entrepreneurialism, humility, and respect What We Offer Competitive benefits: Enjoy a 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting, flexible time off, comprehensive health and dental plans, plus wellness and mental health support through Peloton and Talkspace. A meaningful career: Join a passionate community of over 1,300 employees dedicated to improving lives and driving innovative solutions to complex social challenges. Commitment to growth: Thrive in a non-hierarchical environment that empowers employees to discover, develop and apply their unique talents. For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $150,000–$225,000 per year. This role may also be eligible for additional bonus compensation designed to align total compensation with an employee’s overall contribution to the organization. Our Principles-Based Management™ (PBM) compensation philosophy is grounded in an individualized approach that rewards the long-term value each person creates for the organization. Compensation decisions are informed by a variety of factors, including relevant experience, capabilities, demonstrated skills, role responsibilities, and expected contribution. Consistent with this approach, base salary may vary within or outside of the anticipated range based on these considerations. $150,000 - $225,000 a year Our Values: Working for an organization within the Stand Together philanthropic community is different from many other places. The culture is deeply rooted in Principle Based Management® (PBM®), a framework guided by the principles that drive human progress, such as dignity, openness, and bottom-up empowerment. PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. That is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, and respect. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

item.title: Director Legislative Outreach
item.description: Position Summary This position leads legislative outreach and engagement on standards and technology policy issues. The role monitors federal and state legislative activity affecting standards, provides timely analysis and status updates, and supports the planning and execution of congressional education and outreach programs. The incumbent will build and maintain relationships with key federal and state policy stakeholders, including organizations such as the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) and the National Association of Secretaries of State (NASS). The position also develops strategic messaging and high-impact programs that demonstrate the value of standards in advancing public health, safety, security, innovation, and U.S. economic competitiveness. Essential Functions Monitor and analyze standards- and technology-related legislation, hearings, and policy developments in Congress, and provide regular updates to leadership. Identify opportunities, venues, and stakeholders for congressional outreach and educational programs that highlight the role of standards in addressing national priorities. Develop briefing materials, policy communications, and educational resources that increase legislative awareness of the benefits of standards to public health, safety, security, and economic competitiveness. Build and maintain relationships with state legislative organizations and policymakers to promote understanding of standards and standardization activities. Interface with other ANSI staff to acquire knowledge about various ANSI programs and services and coordinate messaging. Information Security Responsibilities Attend/complete assigned information security training by the designated completion date. Read and adhere to published ISMS policies and procedures. Report timely any observed violations of ISMS policy - or known encroachments on information security - to your department leader and/or the Information Technology Department. Education and Experience Master’s degree preferred; focus on economics, business, public policy, engineering, science or related field a plus A minimum of ten years’ experience, preferably at a nonprofit organization, public interest group, Congressional office or government agency Other Qualifications Communications coursework a plus Further relevant education a plus Familiarity with the standards community and U.S. system Thorough knowledge of technology issues Working knowledge of the legislative process and Congressional operations generally Strong networking skills Strong interpersonal, social media, verbal communication, and writing skills Team player with ability to interact with all levels of the organization A commitment to public service and the protection of others Proficiency in Microsoft 365, including Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and the Internet Starting compensation will be in the $133,400 to $150,900 range, depending on education, experience, and other qualifications. This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice. ANSI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment, and prohibits discrimination of any type because of race, gender identity or expression, color, national origin or ancestry, religion, creed, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, citizenship or authorized alien status, genetics, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other consideration protected by federal, state, or local laws. ANSI policy also prohibits unlawful discrimination based on the perception that anyone has any of those characteristics. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training. Important Notice for Job Seekers: Protect Yourself from Fraudulent Job Postings We are aware of fraudulent job postings falsely claiming to represent our company. These scams may mirror our legitimate job listings and direct candidates to fake interview links or request personal information. Here's how to spot legitimate opportunities: · Verify jobs at www.ansi.org · Apply through our official Workday system at https://ansi.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/ANSI_Careers · We won’t ask for an interview via Zoom links or texts. · We would never ask for payment · We won’t ask for sensitive, personal information early in an application process. · All communication comes from official company emails (@ansi.org). We prioritize your security and use only official channels. If you see a suspicious posting, please report it to the job board.
